Redwood Facilities Group's tags (`janitorial, supplies, services` — a real but unrelated janitorial-category invoice) match the bare `%supplies%` branch, pulling its $1,590 into the total: 450 + 1590 = 2040.00, an exact match to the wrong figure reported. **Suggested fix**: tighten the SQL-generation prompt's category-matching rule to require the full phrase (or a small, deliberately curated set of true synonyms decided per-category) rather than decomposing a multi-word category into independent single-word OR branches — the current behavior effectively treats every word in the user's phrase as its own unscoped filter.

- `[x]` **Gap 242 (BE): category SQL generation inconsistently limits itself to item-description text only, missing vendors identifiable by name or tag** — opened 2026-08-17. Asked *"And logistics or freight costs?"* — answered $200.00 (one Cascade Manufacturing Co freight line item); missed Blue Ridge Logistics entirely ($2,386.31, a vendor literally named "Logistics" with tags `freight, logistics`). **Root cause confirmed from the actual generated SQL**: this query only checks `LOWER(item->>'description') LIKE '%freight%'/'%logist%'/'%shipping%'` via `jsonb_array_elements` — it never checks `vendor_name` or `tags` at all, unlike this same test's turn-1 query (Gap 241, above), which did check `tags`. **Confound disclosed, not hidden**: Blue Ridge Logistics' `items` column was overwritten to a placeholder (`"TEST LINE ITEM EDIT"`, no freight-related text) during this session's own earlier Gap 234 end-to-end verification test — so this specific vendor's miss is partly my own test-data side effect, not purely the app. The query-structure gap is independently real regardless: it's inconsistent with turn 1's query about which columns get checked for a category-style question, and Blue Ridge Logistics' tags (`freight`, `logistics`) are untouched by the data corruption and would have matched had the query checked them. **Suggested fix**: same prompt rule as Gap 241's fix should also standardize which columns a category/keyword question checks (`tags`, `items` description, and `vendor_name`/`customer_name`) — right now different questions produce differently-scoped queries with no visible pattern to which columns get included.

**Gaps 241 + 242 fixed together 2026-08-17/18 — one prompt rule, because they are the same rule seen from two directions** (which text a category phrase is matched against, and how the phrase may be broken up). Both live in `agents/query_agent.py`'s SQL `system_prompt`:

- **Rule 6b (Gap 242)** — one standard shape for every category/subject-matter question: the phrase is matched against the **same four columns** in one parenthesised OR group (`tags`, `items`, `vendor_name`, `customer_name`), never a subset. The rule states outright that checking only item descriptions (or only tags) is a bug, and names the reason — which column a category is identifiable through varies per invoice ("Blue Ridge Logistics" is identifiable by vendor name alone).
- **Rule 6c (Gap 241)** — a multi-word category phrase is **never** decomposed into independent single-word branches: "office supplies" is `'%office supplies%'`, not `('%office%' OR '%supplies%')`, with the janitorial-invoice false positive from this gap's own report given as the worked example. Two categories joined by "or" are two whole phrases, each applied to all four columns. Generic spend words the user tacks on (`costs`, `spend`, `charges`, `invoices`, `bills`, ...) are stripped before the LIKE literal is built, so "freight costs" searches `'%freight%'` — no tag or line item is literally named "freight costs".

**A third defect was found on 2026-08-18 while verifying these two, and is fixed in the same place.** A live run reported `psycopg2.errors.UndefinedFunction: function lower(jsonb) does not exist` on tag/keyword questions. Root cause was the prompt's own worked example: `LOWER(tags) LIKE LOWER('%"hardware"%')`, annotated "(works in both SQLite and Postgres)". It does not — `tags`/`items`/`sa_alerts` are `Column(JSON_VARIANT)` (models.py 82-84) and `JSON_VARIANT` is `sa.JSON().with_variant(JSONB, "postgresql")`, i.e. **JSONB on Postgres, which has no `lower(jsonb)`**. SQLite is untyped and accepts the bare form, which is exactly why the entire mocked unit suite ran green over it. Rule 6 is now split into 6(a) "cast every JSONB column with `CAST(... AS TEXT)` before LOWER/LIKE, never cast the VARCHAR ones" — with the error string quoted in the prompt so the model has the reason — and 6(b) the pre-existing LOWER-both-sides rule; rule 6b's four-column group shows the cast form too. **`CAST(... AS TEXT)` rather than `::text` deliberately**, verified by executing both against both engines: `::text` fixes Postgres and breaks SQLite (`unrecognized token: ":"`), while `CAST` works on both. A repo-wide grep confirmed no other application-code site emitted an uncast `LOWER(tags|items|sa_alerts)`.

**Verified live, before vs after** (two private uvicorn instances — fixed on :8100, deliberately-reverted prompt on :8200 — so the shared :8000 stack stayed free), by `tests/gap6d_jsonb_cast_probe.py` over category-phrase and named-tag question sets: **pre-fix, 13 SQL executions aborted with `function lower(jsonb) does not exist` across 16 chat messages; post-fix, 0 across 32.** Worth recording *why the chat UI never showed this*: all 13 aborts were on attempt 1 and the SQL route's error-feedback retry loop repaired every one of them on attempt 2, so the user-visible answer looked fine while every JSON-column question silently cost an extra LLM round-trip, a failed statement and a session rollback. The probe's own SQL-shape counters read 0 pre-fix for the same reason (they see the post-repair query) — the server log is the ground truth, and both are kept in the evidence dir. Unit tests: `tests/test_chat_sql_quality.py` (32 tests; 4 for the cast, two of which *execute* the predicate against the real SQLite and Postgres engines rather than asserting on prompt text). Full suite green: **616 passed, 0 failed.** Evidence: `docs/test_evidence/gap237_jsonb_cast_2026-08-18/README.md`.

**Scope note, deliberately left open**: rule 6c's phrase-preserving behaviour and rule 6b's four-column group were re-checked live only on the Gap 237 seed tenant and the probe's question set, not re-run against tenant-us's original "$2,040.00 vs $450" and "$200.00" numbers — that reseeded tenant-us data is shared with other concurrent work. The prompt rules are in place and unit-asserted; a tenant-us re-ask is the cleaner end-to-end confirmation if one is wanted.

**Confound cleared 2026-08-17 by functional-tester, ahead of the fix**: reseeded Blue Ridge Logistics' `items`. Confirmed the corruption went further than known — `subtotal` had also been silently overwritten to 200.0, no longer reconciling with the untouched `tax_amount`/`grand_total`. Reverse-solved the real pre-corruption subtotal ($2,225.00, an exact match against the row's stored 7.25% tax rate) and restored 4 realistic freight/logistics line items summing to it; `grand_total`/`tax_amount`/`tags` were untouched throughout and left as-is. Evidence: `docs/test_evidence/gap242_blue_ridge_reseed_2026-08-17/README.md` + `before_after.json`; script `tests/gap242_reseed_blue_ridge.py`. The fix can now be verified against clean data.

- `[x]` **Gap 243 (BE): outbound invoices have the same permanent RAG-indexing gap as Gap 240, on the `NEEDS_REVIEW` side** — opened 2026-08-17, filed separately from Gap 240 per founder direction (same root shape, but a distinct code path worth its own tracking and its own close). `queue_worker/outbound_handlers.py:127` gates the only call to `chroma_client.index_invoice_document()` on `if status == "VERIFIED":` — an outbound invoice that lands `NEEDS_REVIEW` (the outbound equivalent of `AUDIT_REQUIRED`) is never indexed, permanently: confirmed `routers/outbound_audit.py` (the outbound resolve path) has **no call to `index_invoice_document()` anywhere in the file** — grepped directly, zero matches. So a customer-facing invoice a human has to review never becomes searchable via RAG chat even after it's resolved, same shape as Gap 240's inbound finding. **Suggested fix, same shape as Gap 240's corrected fix (see that gap's note on why the naive "backstop on resolve" doesn't work for the inbound side — the outbound resolve path needs the same "index on resolve, regardless of final status" treatment, not a status-gated one)**: call `index_invoice_document()` for `NEEDS_REVIEW` outbound invoices at ingestion time too, and add an indexing call to `routers/outbound_audit.py`'s resolve path keyed on the resolution happening at all, not on which status it resolves to.

  **Fixed 2026-08-17, exactly as suggested.** `queue_worker/outbound_handlers.py` now gates on the same shared `chroma_client.should_index_status()` as inbound, and `routers/outbound_audit.py::resolve_outbound_alert()` got the twin backstop (probe `has_invoice_chunks()` first, index with `customer_name` to match how outbound ingestion passes it through the `vendor_name` parameter, never fail the resolve on a Chroma error). **Worth recording why the "keyed on the resolution happening at all" framing is not just a preference here**: this endpoint never mutates `invoice.status` at all — an outbound resolve is corrections plus alert dismissal only — so unlike inbound there is no status transition available to key on even in principle. Confirmed by direct read of the endpoint, not assumed. **Found and corrected while fixing**: `tests/test_direction_aware_chat.py::test_needs_review_outbound_invoice_skips_rag_indexing` was an existing test that *asserted this bug* (it locked in Feature 6.1's original `VERIFIED`-only gate). Inverted to `..._also_triggers_rag_indexing`, and paired with a new `test_unextracted_outbound_invoice_is_not_rag_indexed` so widening the gate stays bounded — a FAILED extraction has no usable content and still stays out. **Also corrected**: `feature_2.1_vendor_flow_ingestion.md` Task 2.1.3 still claimed "No RAG indexing — out of scope for ingestion", stale since Feature 6.1 Task 6.1.3 added it; the spec body now reflects what is actually built. Verified against real data: tenant-us's 1 `NEEDS_REVIEW` outbound invoice was among the 3 absent from its pre-fix collection (see Gap 240's `7 = |COMPLETED| + |VERIFIED|` arithmetic) and is present after the re-embed migration. `tests/test_rag.py::test_outbound_resolve_backfills_rag_index_for_an_unindexed_invoice` added; full suite green (609 passed, 0 failed).

- `[x]` **Gap 244 (BE): RAG semantic vector search is not functionally contributing to retrieval — real embedding distances are far outside the enforced relevance threshold for every query tested, so matches only succeed via a literal-keyword fallback** — opened 2026-08-17, escalated from a secondary finding in Gap 240 into its own gap per founder direction, since it's a distinct root cause needing its own investigation and applies identically to **both inbound and outbound** (both flows share the same `chroma_client.py` indexing/query functions — this is not two separate bugs).

  > ⚠️ **ROOT-CAUSE CORRECTION, 2026-08-17 — read this before the original analysis below.** Items **2** and **4** of the root cause as originally filed (the "measured L2 norm ≈ 1.82" and the "L2 distances of 5.8–7.3") are **factually wrong as statements about the real model**. They are measurements of the **mock** embedding path. See the "Corrected root cause" block after item 5. The gap's *conclusion* — that semantic similarity was contributing nothing and only the keyword fallback was working — is nonetheless correct, and the fix shipped in full. Items 1, 3 and 5 stand.

  **Root cause, confirmed by direct measurement, not inferred**:
  1. `chroma_client.py::get_embedding_model()` loads `BAAI/bge-m3` via `sentence-transformers`, a model whose intended similarity metric is **cosine** (i.e., it expects comparisons on unit-normalized vectors).
  2. `get_embeddings()` (`chroma_client.py:66`) calls `model.encode(texts, convert_to_numpy=True)` **without `normalize_embeddings=True`** — measured directly against the real model: returned vectors have L2 norm ≈ **1.82**, not 1.0.
  3. None of the three `client.get_or_create_collection(...)` call sites in `chroma_client.py` pass `metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"}` — Chroma defaults to raw (squared) L2 distance, which is unbounded and scales with vector magnitude, not a 0–2 cosine-equivalent range.
  4. Net effect, measured directly against tenant-us's real collection: genuine matches (a vendor's own indexed chunk against a query naming that vendor's category) return **L2 distances of 5.8–7.3**, evaluated against the **0.4** relevance threshold set in `query_invoice_chunks()` (Gap 21). The threshold was almost certainly calibrated assuming a bounded cosine/normalized-L2 distance space (where 0.4 is a sensible, fairly tight cutoff) — against raw unnormalized L2 it is unreachable by construction, for **every** query, not just the ones this session happened to test.
  5. The only reason RAG retrieval works at all today is `query_invoice_chunks()`'s literal-keyword-overlap override (`chunk["keyword_score"] >= min_k_score` lets a candidate through regardless of vector distance) — confirmed by this session's category-browsing test, where every correct RAG answer (manufacturing/tooling, janitorial) matched via literal keyword overlap with the vendor name or line-item text, never via genuine semantic similarity. A question phrased without enough literal word-overlap with the source document text has no retrieval path at all right now.

  **Corrected root cause (measured 2026-08-17 while implementing the fix)**:

  - **Item 2 is wrong.** Real `BAAI/bge-m3`, loaded live (2.2 GB into the HF cache), returns vectors of L2 norm **1.0**, not 1.82 — with or without `normalize_embeddings=True` — because its own `modules.json` already ends in a `sentence_transformers.models.Normalize` module (index 2, after Transformer and Pooling). The model was never the problem.
  - **`1.82` is the signature of the mock path.** `MOCK_EMBEDDINGS=true` is set in this repo's local `.env`, and `get_embeddings()`'s mock branch returned `random.uniform(-0.1, 0.1)` over 1024 dims: measured mean norm **1.847** (range 1.814–1.942), and mock-vs-mock squared-L2 distance **6.55** — squarely inside the reported 5.8–7.3 band. **Item 4's entire measured range was therefore a mock-path artifact**; no real-model distance was ever in it.
  - **Items 1, 3 and 5 are real and were independently re-confirmed.** Chroma really did default every collection to `l2` (verified: all three live local collections read back `space=l2`), the 0.4 threshold really was unreachable in that space, and retrieval really was running entirely on the keyword fallback.
  - **The fix is still worth shipping in full, on the strength of item 3 rather than item 2.** Verified live against **chromadb 1.5.9**: passing `metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"}` to `get_or_create_collection()` for a collection that **already exists** silently returns it still on `l2` — no error, no warning. Re-embedding is therefore mandatory, not optional, and a migration script had to be written.
  - **Blast radius, measured, and worth knowing for other gaps' evidence**: the L2 norm of every vector stored in every live local collection, before anything was migrated, was IEQ-India **1.8604**, IEQ-US **1.8570**, IEQ-Europe **1.8557** — all the mock signature, all on `space=l2`. **Not one real-model embedding existed in the local Chroma stack, so real-model RAG retrieval had never been exercised locally by any test before this pass.** Consequences: Gap 240's Chroma-vs-Postgres diff **survives intact** (it is about which invoice ids are present, which is independent of vector content, and is independently corroborated by the code gate and by the `7 = |COMPLETED| + |VERIFIED|` arithmetic); the category-browsing test's "every correct answer came via keyword overlap" **survives and is now fully explained** (with random vectors the vector channel carries no signal by construction, so the keyword fallback was mathematically the only thing that could have worked); Gaps 241/242 are SQL-route findings and never involved embeddings.
  - **Process lesson**: the mock branch now normalizes its vectors too, specifically so unnormalized mock output can never again be mistaken for a real-model measurement. `tests/test_rag.py`'s new coverage is explicitly labelled structural-only for the same reason, with retrieval-quality claims kept in `docs/test_evidence/` where the embedding mode of each measurement is stated.

  **Immediate, model-independent fix (do this regardless of any model decision below)**: add `normalize_embeddings=True` to the `model.encode()` call, set `hnsw:space: "cosine"` on collection creation (a new setting on new collections — existing collections would need re-embedding to switch space, since Chroma's HNSW index is built for one space at creation time), and re-derive the relevance threshold empirically against real bounded cosine distances instead of carrying the old 0.4 value forward unchanged. This alone is expected to make genuine semantic matches reachable without changing the underlying model, and should be tried and measured before spending on a model upgrade.

  **Separate question, needs a market decision — self-hosted `BAAI/bge-m3` vs. a hosted embedding API.** Researched current options (Aug 2026):
  - **Recommended: Azure OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large`.** This codebase already holds a live Azure OpenAI resource/credentials for the chat LLM (`AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT`/`AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY` in `config.py`) — adding an embedding deployment on the same resource needs no new vendor relationship, no new procurement/security review, and reuses the existing auth/billing path. Strong general retrieval quality, well-documented, low integration risk given what's already wired up.
  - **Highest measured retrieval quality, if a new vendor is acceptable: Voyage AI (`voyage-3-large` / `voyage-3.5`).** Independently benchmarked as leading MTEB retrieval scores in 2026 comparisons, reported ~14% ahead of OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` and ~8% ahead of Cohere `embed-v4` on NDCG@10, with a 32K context window (useful for longer multi-page invoices). Worth it only if retrieval precision remains a business priority after the immediate normalization/cosine fix above is measured — a new vendor relationship is real integration + security-review cost this repo hasn't taken on before for RAG specifically.
  - **Keep self-hosted `BAAI/bge-m3` (fix the normalization/space bug only, no model change)** if avoiding both a new vendor and added per-token API cost is the priority — 2026 comparisons still list it as "a practical default" for self-hosting, and it may perform adequately once the actual bug (not the model) is fixed.
  - **Not recommended for this use case**: Google Gemini Embedding (multilingual/multimodal-leading, but invoices here are financial documents, not the video/audio-multimodal case Gemini is differentiated for) and Cohere `embed-v4` (multilingual leader, but Voyage AI outperforms it on retrieval accuracy specifically, which is the more relevant axis for invoice line-item/category search).

  **Suggested path**: ship the normalization/cosine-space fix first (cheap, no vendor change, likely closes most of the gap on its own), re-measure real distances and retrieval quality against a re-run of this session's category-browsing test, and only then decide whether a hosted-model upgrade (Azure OpenAI `text-embedding-3-large` first choice) is still worth it. **Applies to both inbound and outbound** — `chroma_client.py` is shared, no separate outbound work needed for this specific fix.

  **Decision 2026-08-17 (founder-directed, per architect's independent second opinion)**: fix the config bug first, keep `BAAI/bge-m3`, do **not** add Voyage AI now. Architect's reasoning, given directly to the founder and accepted: BGE-M3 is a mainstream, competitive model — the measured 1.82 norm is evidence it worked correctly, the vectors were just never normalized before comparison. Swapping to a hosted model (Voyage or Azure OpenAI) right now would very likely *appear* to fix retrieval, because hosted APIs return pre-normalized vectors by default — but that would misattribute a free one-line config fix to a new recurring per-token vendor cost. Scope for this pass is therefore strictly: (1) `normalize_embeddings=True` on `get_embeddings()`'s `model.encode()` call, (2) `metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"}` on all three `get_or_create_collection()` call sites (existing collections need re-embedding, since Chroma fixes the HNSW distance space at creation), (3) re-derive the 0.4 relevance threshold empirically against real bounded cosine distances rather than carrying the old value forward, (4) re-run this session's category-browsing test live to confirm real semantic matches now pass without the keyword-overlap fallback carrying them. The Voyage/Azure-OpenAI model-upgrade question is deferred, not closed — revisit only if retrieval quality is still short after this fix, and only against a clean baseline this fix establishes.

  **Fixed 2026-08-17, all four scoped items shipped.** `BAAI/bge-m3` kept, no new vendor, per the decision above.

  1. **`normalize_embeddings=True`** on `get_embeddings()`'s `model.encode()`. Against the real model this is a **no-op** (see the root-cause correction) and is stated as an explicit contract so a future model swap can't silently reintroduce unnormalized vectors. The **mock branch was also normalized**, which is the change that carries real weight here.
  2. **`metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"}`** on every `get_or_create_collection()` call site, via `_collection_metadata()`. Added `_collection_space()` and `_to_cosine_distance()` so the threshold means the same thing on a not-yet-migrated collection — for unit vectors squared-L2 = 2 × cosine distance *exactly*, and the measurements confirm it (every `l2` figure is precisely double its cosine twin: 0.9709/0.4854, 0.7646/0.3823, 0.8263/0.4131, …), which is itself an independent confirmation that the real model's output is unit norm.
  3. **Threshold re-derived empirically → `RELEVANCE_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD = 0.49` cosine** (was 0.4). Not chosen by intuition: the 8 category-browsing questions were embedded with the real model against real invoice PDFs, twice — once over tenant-us's 10 invoices, once over all 30 invoices of the three InvoiceEQ tenants so the false-positive floor was estimated off ~3× the negatives. Both runs produced the same separation band: **hardest genuine match that is separable at all = 0.4749** ("janitorial or cleaning services" → Redwood Facilities Group); **best false positive on a deliberately-absent category = 0.5062** ("legal or attorney fees" → Fieldstone Analytics). **0.49 is the midpoint**, the maximally drift-tolerant point between catching real matches and still honestly answering "no match". The one genuine match 0.49 misses is CMC-330217 at **0.5331** (a single $200 freight line on an otherwise-manufacturing invoice) — it sits *above* the false-positive floor, so no threshold can admit it without also admitting fabricated matches; it is left to the keyword pass, which is now a genuine second channel rather than the only working one.
  4. **Category-browsing test re-run live** through the shipped `query_invoice_chunks()`, with a real before/after on the real stack.

  **Measured before/after** (full data: `docs/test_evidence/gap244_rag_retrieval_2026-08-17/`):

  | | before (unmigrated tenant IEQ-Europe: `space=l2`, mock vectors) | after (migrated tenant-us: `space=cosine`, real vectors) |
  |---|---|---|
  | stored-vector L2 norm | ~1.857 | **1.000000** exactly |
  | distance on a genuine match | **2.3610** — 4.8× the threshold | **0.3823 – 0.4749** |
  | what carried the match | `matched_by=keyword`, always | `matched_by=vector` on 2 of 6 turns, `vector+keyword` on 4 |
  | absent categories | — | **no match returned**, correctly, on both |

  Post-fix, 6/6 real categories retrieve their correct vendor and 2/2 deliberately-absent categories honestly return nothing. **The decisive result: *"What about printing costs?"* matched Apex Print Solutions at 0.3924 with `keyword_score = 0`** — the document says "Print", the question says "printing", so there is zero literal overlap and the keyword fallback could not have carried it at any threshold. That match is pure semantic similarity, which is exactly what this gap said was missing. (Apex is also `AUDIT_REQUIRED`, so pre-fix it wasn't in the index at all — one turn proving Gaps 240 and 244 together.) Turn 6, Titan Steel at 0.3823 with kw=1 below the min_k_score of 2, is the same proof a second time. **Honest caveat**: at 0.49 several turns also admit non-expected chunks under the threshold (turn 6 admits 5) — recall-oriented by design, since the LLM filters the passed chunks afterwards, and the reason 0.49 sits at the band's midpoint rather than its top. Not a regression: pre-fix those questions returned only keyword hits or nothing.

  **To make the claim assertable at all**, each chunk returned by `query_invoice_chunks()` now also carries `keyword_score` and `matched_by` (`vector` / `keyword` / `vector+keyword`) — purely additive; `agents/query_agent.py` reads only `document` and `metadata` (verified by reading it, not assumed) and was not touched.

  **Migration**: `scripts/reembed_chroma_collections.py` — drops and rebuilds each tenant's collection as cosine and re-indexes everything passing `should_index_status()`, making it the backfill for Gaps 240 and 243 as well; also does Gap 239 orphan detection/pruning at collection and chunk granularity, has a `--prune-only` audit mode that never loads the model, refuses `--apply` while `MOCK_EMBEDDINGS` is on, and reads each rebuilt collection's space back to confirm it really landed on `cosine` rather than assuming the metadata took. Procedure (pre-flight, ordering, rollback, verification) documented in `docs/feature_6_rag.md` §"Gap 244 re-embed migration procedure". **Run so far against tenant-us only**, deliberately — the other tenants were left unmigrated to preserve the before-state control above and to avoid disturbing a concurrently-used local stack. **The remaining tenants still need the migration run before their RAG chat benefits**; until then `_to_cosine_distance()` keeps their threshold semantics correct, but their stored vectors are still mock.

  **Verified**: 26 tests added in `tests/test_rag.py` (unit-norm embeddings, `_to_cosine_distance` rescaling, cosine-space collection creation, `matched_by` channel reporting, threshold pinned inside its derived band, `should_index_status()` in both directions, and the resolve backstops); an existing test asserting the Gap 243 bug inverted in `tests/test_direction_aware_chat.py`; full BE suite green — **609 passed, 0 failed, 5 deselected, run three times** against a real local Postgres/Redis/Chroma stack. Also fixed a **pre-existing, order-dependent** suite failure surfaced by this work: `test_rag_citations_drop_ids_with_no_matching_invoice_row` asks a fixed question as the fixed `MOCK_TENANT_ID`, and the Task 6.11 answer cache lives in the *real shared* local Redis with a 1hr TTL and no per-test namespace, so a `chat_answer_cache:00000000-…:which vendors have freight charges?` entry left by an earlier run was served instead of the mocked RAG path and the test asserted against a stranger's citations (confirmed by reading the live key out of Redis). Fixed hermetically by forcing a cache miss in the test, not by clearing shared state.

  Sources: [Best Embedding Model for RAG 2026 — Milvus](https://milvus.io/blog/choose-embedding-model-rag-2026.md), [Voyage 3.5 vs OpenAI vs Cohere Embedding Models 2026](https://www.buildmvpfast.com/blog/best-embedding-model-comparison-voyage-openai-cohere-2026), [Best Embedding Models for RAG in 2026 — StackAI](https://www.stackai.com/insights/best-embedding-models-for-rag-in-2026-a-comparison-guide)

## Feature 19 — Support Ticket Engine, AI Support Agent & Notification Email Dispatch (2026-08-17)

Full BE design + verification record: `docs/feature_19_support_tickets_and_notifications.md`.

> **Renumbered 2026-08-18, before merge.** These three entries were originally filed on this branch as Gaps **240/241/242 (BE)**. Master independently opened its own Gaps 240–245 (BE) for the chat SQL-generation / RAG-indexing defects while this branch was unmerged, and a `git merge-tree` dry run confirmed this file **auto-merges without raising a conflict** — which would have silently produced two Gap 240s, two Gap 241s and two Gap 242s. This branch's set is the newer and still-unmerged one, so it was moved to **246/247/248** rather than master's. No other gap number in this file was touched.

  - **`main.py`** — `support.router` registered at `/api/v1`.
  - **`tests/test_support.py`** (new) — **22/22 tests passing** (in-memory SQLite, mock email dispatch):
    - Contact form: valid payload → 201, ticket number format, DB persistence, field validation (name/email/message required, email format, message length), unknown category/urgency coercion.
    - AI Support Chat: documentation query returns guidance, error keywords trigger smart escalation card, human help triggers escalation, empty input validation.
    - App ticket: 201 response, `TICK-` format, chat transcript persisted, `HELP_CHATBOT` source stored.
    - Ticket list: empty list, tenant's own tickets returned.
    - Email: dispatch mock called once, `RuntimeError` from dispatch → still 201 with `email_dispatched: false`.

- `[x]` **Gap 367 (BE): Support Assistant (`agents/support_agent.py`) needs RAG-based accuracy tuning — currently answers from a hardcoded keyword-matched knowledge base, not vector search** — opened 2026-09-02, sourced from an external defect review, item **H-04 (A) — Support Assistant RAG Accuracy Tuning** ("Enhance the vector search / prompt context for the Support Assistant to improve resolution of domain questions"). **Gap number collision-checked fresh**: repo-wide max was 366 (BE, Feature 26). **Built and verified 2026-09-02.**
  - **What existed before this fix, confirmed by reading the code, not assumed.** `evaluate_support_query()` in `agents/support_agent.py` was a deterministic keyword-scoring + regex matcher over two hardcoded module-level tables, `KNOWLEDGE_TOPICS` (12 topics) and `ERROR_TRIGGERS` — no LLM call, no embedding, no vector store anywhere in the module. This is a **different agent and a different retrieval path** from the main Chat Assistant's `agents/query_agent.py` (Feature 6 — SAGE), which already has hybrid vector+keyword retrieval, cosine-space Chroma collections, and reranking built up through Gaps 21/22/244/278/365 — none of that work touched `support_agent.py`.
  - **Scope decision (founder-approved before implementation, per this file's founder-gate rule): hybrid vector search only, not full RAG.** The keyword pass is completely untouched and still decides first, exactly as before. Only a query that scores **zero** keyword hits, and is not an error trigger or an explicit human-help request (both checked first and left exactly as deterministic as before), now gets one more chance: `_vector_match_topic()` embeds the query and queries a new shared, non-tenant Chroma collection (`support_knowledge_topics`, cosine space) seeded from each topic's title + curated keywords, reusing `chroma_client.py`'s existing client/embedding singletons rather than building new infra. A confident match (distance ≤ `SUPPORT_RELEVANCE_DISTANCE_THRESHOLD = 0.35`, a deliberately conservative starting point — there is no labelled dataset to derive it empirically the way Gap 244 did, and this is documented in-code as needing live tuning, not presented as scientifically grounded) returns that topic's existing pre-written `guidance` text; a Chroma/embedding failure degrades to the pre-existing miss rather than raising. **No LLM call was added anywhere.**
  - **Verified — `tests/test_support.py`: 75 passed** (all pre-existing cases unmodified + 5 new in `TestSupportAgentVectorFallback`), run in isolation with `MOCK_EMBEDDINGS=true`. The new tests prove, not just assert: random mock vectors never produce a false-positive match (why every pre-existing miss-test still passes unmodified); a zero-keyword-overlap paraphrase resolves to the correct topic under controlled (monkeypatched) embeddings; a call-counter proof that the vector step never runs when a keyword match or error trigger already decided the answer; a Chroma/embedding failure degrades to the existing miss. **Full backend suite re-run, 2026-09-02: 25 failed, 1773 passed, 3 skipped, 4 errors (177.65s) — every failure checked individually and traced to pre-existing causes unrelated to this change** (local Postgres missing a migrated column across several unrelated `*_on_postgres` tests; Gap 354's already-documented `test_rag.py` failure; unrelated benchmark-telemetry/ops-workbook/connector tests). `tests/test_support.py` contributed zero failures. **Not done, not claimed**: no live run against the real `BAAI/bge-m3` model — real-world semantic match quality (as opposed to the retrieval mechanism being wired correctly) is unmeasured, and the 0.35 threshold is exactly what such a run would need to validate or correct. No Postgres/DB code was touched by this change, so Hard Rule 2 does not apply here.
  - Full design record and as-built detail: `feature_19_support_tickets_and_notifications.md` Task 19.3.

## Feature 19 — security findings on the public contact endpoint (2026-08-18)

Opened 2026-08-18 from a **read-only** security review of the new unauthenticated contact-form path, filed at `reports/security/2026-08-18-support-contact-endpoint.md` (scoped exception to this repo's normal coding → functional → env-split → load → security order, taken because a merge-readiness review flagged the endpoint). All three were **open and deliberately not fixed in the merge-prep pass that filed them** — that pass was docs-only, and the review's recommendation that they were merge blockers rather than follow-ups was recorded here for the founder to call rather than acted on. **All three have since been fixed on branch `fix/support-contact-security-and-tenant-provisioning` (2026-08-18); see each entry below.** Findings 5–8 of the report (sync-handler threadpool exhaustion — plausible, not load-tested; tenant isolation and SendGrid key handling — both checked, no issue) are still not filed as gaps: 5 and 6 are deliberately deferred and 7–8 need no action. The report now carries a remediation-status block at the top recording exactly that.

- `[x]` **Gap 249 (BE): `POST /api/v1/support/contact` is public, unauthenticated and has no rate limiting or CAPTCHA anywhere in its path, while two other places in the codebase claim it does** — opened 2026-08-18. **Fixed 2026-08-18 in two passes; closed after the second.**

  **Pass 1 (initial fix).** Dual-layer rate limiting and anti-spam: (1) the Next.js proxy (`apps/invoice-website/app/api/contact/route.ts`) enforced an in-memory sliding window of 5 requests / 10 minutes per IP, dropped bot traffic with a silent 201 when the hidden `hp_field` honeypot was populated, and forwarded a client IP header to the backend; (2) the backend (`routers/support.py`) added `_ContactRateLimiter`, an in-memory sliding window on origin IP and email (5 / 5 minutes) returning `429` with `Retry-After: 300`. The contact page (`app/contact/page.tsx`) renders the honeypot and surfaces a retry message on 429.

  **Pass 2 (hardening — this is what actually closes the gap).** An architect review found pass 1 implemented but bypassable, and found a 500 of the same bug class the branch claimed to have fixed. All addressed:
  - **The rate-limit key was fully attacker-controlled.** Both layers took the *leftmost* `X-Forwarded-For` entry — the value the client supplies — so sending a fresh one per request reset both windows and defeated the limiter completely. Trust order is now: `X-Azure-ClientIP` **only** when `X-Azure-FDID` matches a configured `FRONT_DOOR_ID` (unset today, so ignored — Front Door is gated on `customDomainName` in `infra/08-apps.bicep` and is not deployed, making those headers forgeable); then `X-Client-IP`, which the website proxy sets from its own resolution and never forwards from the browser; then the **rightmost** valid `X-Forwarded-For` entry (the hop Container Apps' Envoy ingress actually observed); then the socket peer. `X-Real-IP` is no longer consulted. Every candidate must parse as a real IP via `_parse_ip`, so junk cannot become a rate-limit key.
  - **Limiter state was unbounded and per-replica.** The backend window now lives in Redis (sorted set per key, `EXPIRE` on every write), so it is genuinely shared across the app's 5 replicas and self-bounding. Redis being unreachable degrades to a bounded in-process window (`services/trainer_sessions.py`'s `_get_redis` fallback pattern) that prunes out-of-window keys on every check and caps tracked keys at `_MEMORY_MAX_TRACKED_KEYS` — it does not fail open and does not 500. The `defaultdict` was replaced with an `OrderedDict`, which also stops a rejected lookup from permanently creating a key.
  - **Subject-length 500.** `submit_contact_inquiry` built `f"[{category}] Contact inquiry from {name}"` with `name` capped at 255 but the prefix adding 31–41 more, overflowing `SupportTicket.subject`'s `max_length=255` → Postgres `StringDataRightTruncation` → uncaught 500. Now truncated to `_SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH` at construction (chosen over lowering `name`'s cap so a future prefix-format change cannot reintroduce it).
  - **Honeypot false positives were invisible.** A password manager filling `hp_field` silently discarded a genuine inquiry while telling the user it was received. The proxy now logs a `console.warn` with the trigger value, claimed name/email and user agent so a false-positive pattern is visible in logs; the client-facing response is deliberately unchanged so bots learn nothing.

  **Remaining caveat, stated rather than glossed:** the *website proxy* window is still per-instance and that app scales 0–3 with scale-to-zero, so a cold start wipes it and its effective ceiling is up to `instances x 5`. This is accepted, not overlooked — that layer is best-effort edge shedding, and the authoritative limit is the backend's Redis-backed one. The backend falls back to a per-replica window only while Redis is down.

  **Verification:** full backend suite green — 674 passed, 4 skipped. 28 new tests in `tests/test_support.py` (`TestSubjectLengthOverflow`, `TestClientIpResolution`, `TestRateLimitBypassResistance`, `TestRateLimiterStateBounds`) alongside the original `test_rate_limit_returns_429_after_threshold`. The two regression tests were confirmed to genuinely fail against the pre-fix code, not just pass against the new: reverting the truncation fails the subject tests (256 and 296 chars), and reverting `_get_client_ip` fails `test_rotating_leftmost_forwarded_for_cannot_reset_window` with 201 instead of 429. Subject assertions are on the constructed/stored string's length, because the suite's in-memory SQLite does not enforce `max_length` and a status-only assertion would pass with the bug present. `tsc --noEmit` clean on `invoice-website`. Not deployed to any Azure environment.

  Files: `routers/support.py`, `config.py` (`FRONT_DOOR_ID`), `models.py` (ticket-number format comment), `tests/test_support.py`, `apps/invoice-website/app/api/contact/route.ts`, `apps/invoice-website/app/contact/page.tsx`, `docs/feature_19_support_tickets_and_notifications.md`, `reports/security/2026-08-18-support-contact-endpoint.md`.

- `[x]` **Gap 250 (BE): `services/support_email.py` interpolates attacker-controlled request fields into both email templates with no HTML escaping — an open relay for phishing from the platform's own authenticated sending domain. Highest-severity finding of the review.** — opened 2026-08-18. **Fixed 2026-08-18.** All user-supplied request fields in both email templates (`_ticket_html` and `_receipt_html` in `services/support_email.py`) are now strictly HTML-escaped using Python's `html.escape(..., quote=True)` — covering `user_name`, `company_name`, `user_email` (both display and `mailto:` link), `subject`, and `description`. Subjects are sanitized against newline injection (`\r`/`\n` stripped). Input length validation added to `ContactInquiryRequest` and `AppTicketRequest` for `name` and `company` (max 255 chars), preventing unhandled DB `StringDataRightTruncation` 500s. Covered by automated tests `test_html_in_name_is_escaped_in_receipt_email`, `test_html_in_name_is_escaped_in_staff_alert`, `test_html_in_description_is_escaped_in_staff_alert`, `test_html_in_company_is_escaped_in_staff_alert`, `test_name_over_255_chars_is_rejected`, `test_company_over_255_chars_is_rejected` in `tests/test_support.py`. Files: `services/support_email.py`, `routers/support.py`, `tests/test_support.py`.

- `[x]` **Gap 251 (BE): the ticket-number keyspace is 9,000 values per year, and exhausting it takes the contact form down with an uncaught 500** — opened 2026-08-18. **Fixed 2026-08-18.** `_generate_ticket_number()` updated to use cryptographic randomness `secrets.token_hex(4).upper()` yielding 8 uppercase hex characters (4.29 billion distinct values per year per prefix), expanding keyspace by ~477,000x and eliminating enumeration risk. Ticket format: `INQ-YYYY-XXXXXXXX` / `TICK-YYYY-XXXXXXXX`. If exhaustion retries fail, `_unique_ticket_number()` now raises `HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="Ticket generation service temporarily busy — please retry.")` rather than an unhandled `RuntimeError` crashing the endpoint with a 500. Covered by automated tests `test_ticket_number_uses_hex_format` and `test_ticket_generation_exhaustion_returns_503_not_500` in `tests/test_support.py`. Files: `routers/support.py`, `tests/test_support.py`.

- `[x]` **Gap 252 (BE): Chat (and every other request) fails against the deployed dev backend because the readiness probe checks a path that doesn't exist, so the current revision never becomes ready and stays pinned to 100% traffic** — found 2026-08-18, user-reported ("chat is giving failed to response"). Root cause, confirmed directly against the live `ca-invoice-be-dev` Container App and its replicas (not guessed): the app's Readiness probe is configured to `GET /health/readiness` on port 8000, but this FastAPI app only implements `GET /health` — `/health/readiness` 404s every 10s, confirmed continuously in the live container logs. Azure Container Apps will not mark a replica ready until its readiness probe passes, so revision `ca-invoice-be-dev--0000048` (deployed 2026-08-18 09:06 UTC) sits at `runningState: ActivationFailed`, `healthState: Unhealthy`, replica `ready: false`, while `az containerapp ingress traffic show` confirms it still holds **100% of traffic** as the latest revision — so requests routed to it, including chat, fail. **Infra-drift finding, not a bicep bug at the time this was written**: grepped this repo's entire `infra/` and `.github/` trees for `health/readiness` and found zero references — this probe was configured directly on the live Azure resource (portal or manual `az containerapp update`), not through this repo's IaC at the time. **Stale as of 2026-08-18, corrected**: `infra/modules/compute/invoice-be.bicep` now DOES declare `path: '/health/readiness'` explicitly as the Readiness probe — it landed via the Feature 19→20 observability branch merge the same day, after this line was originally written. The durable fix (a real `/health/readiness` endpoint in `main.py`, checking Postgres + Redis) has also landed via that same merge. **Also corrected**: the tracker's Feature 19/20 entry above claimed a "CI/CD post-deploy health verification gate" for this environment — false at the time for dev. Only `deploy-prod.yml` had a post-deploy health check; `deploy-dev.yml`/`_deploy-service.yml` had none, which is the reason this outage held 100% of traffic for hours with no automated signal — closed separately as Gap 258.

  **Closed 2026-08-19/20**: live-confirmed `Running`/`Healthy` on `ca-invoice-be-dev` across roughly a dozen separate deploys through the rest of this session (`--0000055`, `--0000056`, `--0000059`, and others), independently re-checked via `az containerapp revision list` after essentially every push, not just once. No recurrence of the original readiness-probe failure at any point. Gap 258 (dev post-deploy health gate) now exists and has already fired for real once — see that gap's entry for the false-positive it caught and the fix that followed, itself real evidence the gate (and by extension this fix) works as intended.

- `[x]` **Gap 253 (BE): Chat SQL route has no line-item-level extraction — a question about one specific line item returns the whole invoice's grand total instead** — found 2026-08-18, user-reported live example. Asked *"what is the current training amount"* / *"i want the amount only for training and onboarding from the total invoice"* against an invoice with two line items (Cloud Storage $765.36, Training & Onboarding $29,302.94) plus 18% tax, grand total $35,480.59. Chat answered **$35,480.59** both times — the invoice's full `grand_total`, including the unrelated Cloud Storage line and tax — not the correct **$29,302.94** (the Training & Onboarding line's own `amount`). **Root cause, confirmed from the actual generated SQL**: `agents/query_agent.py`'s only category/keyword pattern (rule 6b) is invoice-level — find invoices where `items`/`tags`/`vendor_name`/`customer_name` mention the keyword, then `SUM(grand_total)` across those invoices. There is no rule at all for reaching into the `items` JSONB array and extracting/summing just the matching line item's own `amount`, so any question asking for a specific line item's figure (not "which invoices relate to X") falls back to this invoice-level pattern and silently includes unrelated lines and tax. **Suggested fix**: add a second SQL pattern using `jsonb_array_elements(items)` to unnest line items into rows, filter on each item's own `description`, and select/sum only the matching items' own `description`/`quantity`/`unit_price`/`amount` fields (not the invoice's `grand_total`) — **correction 2026-08-18: no such precedent actually exists** — Gap 241/242's fix text above mentions `jsonb_array_elements` as an example SQL shape in this tracker's prose, but a repo-wide grep of `agents/query_agent.py` and every other `.py` file in `invoice-be` for `jsonb_array_elements`/`json_each` returns zero real occurrences. This would be the **first** JSONB-unnest query written anywhere in this codebase, not an adaptation of an existing one — treat it as new, unproven ground (including for SQLite, which has no `jsonb_array_elements` equivalent and would need its own `json_each`-based path), not a copy-paste of a working pattern. The prompt needs a rule distinguishing "give me this line's own number" (line-item extraction) from "which invoices are about this category" (existing invoice-level rule, unchanged) — that disambiguation, not just the SQL syntax, is the real design work. **Response formatting requirement, per founder direction**: a line-item answer should render as `{description}: {qty} units × ${unit_price} = ${amount}`, one line per matched item; if more than one line item matches (same invoice or across invoices), list each one that way and add a total underneath only when there's more than one. **Fixed 2026-08-19** — see `docs/feature_6_rag.md` "Rule 6d" for the full design. What shipped, in `agents/query_agent.py`: (1) **new rule 6d, dialect-conditioned at prompt-build time.** `_sql_dialect_name(db_session)` reads the live bind's dialect and `_line_item_rule()` renders exactly one of `_LINE_ITEM_RULE_POSTGRES` / `_LINE_ITEM_RULE_SQLITE` into the SQL system prompt, so the model is never shown syntax the bound engine cannot parse. This is the same mechanism rule 6(a) already settled for `CAST(... AS TEXT)` — teach one correct form per engine, never emit dialect-specific SQL and repair it afterwards. **An intermediate implementation did the opposite** (a regex rewriter inside `execute_generated_sql()` translating `jsonb_array_elements`/`->>`/`::numeric` into SQLite at execution time); it was **deleted rather than patched** — it can only ever cover the exact syntactic shapes it was written against, while the model is free to emit any equivalent one. (2) **NULL / non-array `items` guard, taught in the rule for both engines.** `items` is nullable and machine-populated, and un-nesting it unguarded aborts the query for the *whole tenant* off one bad row (verified by hand against SQLite 3.50.4: `json_each('not json')` → `OperationalError: malformed JSON`; Postgres `jsonb_array_elements` raises on a scalar/object the same way) — and each abort burns an attempt of the 3-try repair loop. Both variants therefore wrap the argument: `jsonb_array_elements(CASE WHEN jsonb_typeof(items) = 'array' THEN items ELSE '[]'::jsonb END)` / `json_each(CASE WHEN json_valid(items) AND json_type(items) = 'array' THEN items ELSE '[]' END)`. Guarding via the join's `ON` clause was tested and **rejected** — with `LEFT JOIN` SQLite still evaluates `json_each` before applying `ON` and aborts anyway. (3) **`->>` is native SQLite (3.38+)**, so the SQLite variant uses `item.value ->> 'field'` with no cast; the `.value` matters and is called out explicitly in the prompt, because `json_each(items) AS item` aliases the *table* json_each returns, not the element. (4) **Rule 7 compliance**: 6d selects `currency` in both the detail and the aggregate shape, the aggregate groups by it, and the summary-prompt format is now `{line_description}: {line_qty} units × {currency} {line_unit_price} = {currency} {line_amount}` using the row's own currency — the founder-requested format above hardcoded `$`, which is exactly what FE Gap 183 is on file for. (5) **Rule 9 gained an explicit FROM-clause exception**: this gap's own reported phrasing ("the amount only for training and onboarding **from the total invoice**") is a narrowing follow-up, so 6d and 9 fire together; rule 9 previously fixed only the WHERE clause and said nothing about FROM, which reads as "keep the previous invoice-level FROM" — i.e. return the grand total again. It now authorises adding the line-item join (and only that) while every tenant/invoice-identifying predicate still carries over verbatim. (6) **`_harvest_invoice_ids_via_companion_query()` un-broken for 6d.** It bailed on any `\bjoin\b` in the reconstructed tail, and every 6d query has one — so `result_invoice_ids` came back empty for *every* line-item answer, silently disabling the FE's "which invoice was wrong?" triage picker (Gap 231) and the Gap 237 step-3 hedge (which needs `current_count > 0` to fire). The un-nest join is now whitelisted **by shape** (`_UNNEST_JOIN_RHS`) and the companion query rebuilt as `SELECT DISTINCT invoice.id` — it multiplies rows per invoice but never changes which invoices match; a join to any real table still bails exactly as before. Rule 6d correspondingly tells the model **not** to select `invoice.id` (raw UUIDs in the user-facing results table), since identity is recovered here instead. **Verification**: 12 tests in `tests/test_chat_sql_quality.py` (38 passed / 6 skipped in that file), of which the load-bearing ones *execute* the taught SQL — extracted verbatim out of the prompt constant, so a divergence between what is taught and what is tested is impossible — against the real SQLite engine over the gap's own reported data (Cloud Storage 765.36 + Training & Onboarding 29,302.94 inside a 35,480.59 grand total, plus a NULL-`items` row and a not-JSON-at-all row): returns **29,302.94** only, with the Cloud Storage line absent and the grand total never surfaced. Multi-currency aggregate verified separately (`{"USD": 29502.94, "INR": 50.0}`, grouped, never summed across). Full BE suite: **691 passed, 2 failed, 6 skipped** — both failures are `tests/test_connectors.py` Salesforce OAuth tests needing a local Redis on :6379, confirmed identical on a stashed clean tree, unrelated to this change. **Postgres half closed 2026-08-19 (Gap 255):** `test_taught_line_item_sql_runs_on_postgres` (both parametrized cases) and `test_recommended_cast_form_runs_on_postgres` **passed** against Docker Postgres on `localhost:5433` (`invoice-postgres-local` via `docker-compose.yml`) — rule 6d's Postgres form is now executed evidence on both engines, not asserted-only. Live functional-tester repro (the three scenarios in `.claude/tasklists/senior-dev-gap253-line-item-sql-extraction.md`'s handoff section) is still outstanding; flush the 1hr answer cache before re-testing live — there is no `flush_answer_cache()` helper in `query_agent.py` (only `get_cached_answer`/`set_cached_answer`/`_cache_key`); the existing flush paths are `routers/chat.py::_invalidate_chat_answer_cache()` and `routers/trainer.py::_invalidate_chat_answer_cache()`, or delete the Redis key `chat_answer_cache:{tenant_id}:{normalized question}` directly.

- `[x]` **Gap 254 (BE): Help Center AI Support Assistant answers only a narrow slice of real questions, and presents every miss as a diagnosed incident requiring escalation** — found 2026-08-18, user-reported ("help agent was telling everything not supported"). Two distinct causes confirmed, not one: (1) **BE Gap 252's outage was live at the time** and would independently produce this symptom — every backend call including `/api/v1/support/chat` was failing, though the frontend's outage message ("temporary connection issue communicating with the troubleshooting service") is textually distinguishable from this gap's fallback message, so which one a given user actually saw can be confirmed by the exact wording. (2) **A real, separate defect exists in the assistant's own logic, independently reproducible against a fully healthy backend**: `agents/support_agent.py`'s `KNOWLEDGE_TOPICS` matcher does raw substring matching (`kw in lower_query`) with keywords as short as 2-3 characters, not word-boundary matching. Tested 24 realistic product questions against the real matcher — **11 of 24 fell through to the generic "raise a ticket" fallback** (upload, delete, file formats/limits, bulk upload, user invites, usage/dashboard, data retention, OCR correction, "what is SAGE") and **4 more matched the wrong article via a substring collision**: "What does the **conf-id-ence** score mean?" and "Can I **prov-id-e** feedback?" both hit the `"id"` keyword and return the password-reset article (first in the topic list, so it's the de facto wrong-answer default on any tie); "stuck in **pro**cessing" hits `"pro"` and returns the pricing guide; "**data** encrypted at rest" hits `"data"` and returns the CSV-export guide. Only 7 topics exist total, matching the four hardcoded prompt chips in `SupportChatWindow.tsx` — the demo path works, most of the real question space does not. Compounding this: the fallback path unconditionally sets `suggest_escalation=True`, so an unanswered question renders the same red "Issue Diagnosis & Recommended Escalation" card as a genuine detected error, rather than an honest "I don't have an article for that." `evaluate_support_query()` also accepts a `history` parameter and never reads it, so a natural follow-up ("how do I do that?") always misses regardless. **Suggested fix**: word-boundary matching with a sensible minimum keyword length (kills the substring-collision class outright); a materially expanded topic set covering ingestion/upload, invoice statuses, dashboard/analytics, user management, retention/security, and file limits; a distinct low-confidence "no article for this, try the Knowledge Base search or here's where to look" response path that does not trigger the incident-card styling; actually reading `history` for follow-ups. **Fixed 2026-08-19, with one sub-feature deliberately descoped — hence `[~]`, not `[x]`.** See `docs/feature_19_support_tickets_and_notifications.md` for the full resolution order. What shipped in `agents/support_agent.py`: (1) **word-boundary matching with a 3-character minimum** (`_score_topic()`, `MIN_KEYWORD_LENGTH`), which kills the `"id"`-in-"confidence" / `"pro"`-in-"processing" substring-collision class outright; the `"id"` keyword itself is gone from `account_auth`. (2) **Five new topics** — `ingestion_upload`, `invoice_statuses`, `dashboard_analytics`, `user_management`, `security_retention` — taking the set from 7 to 12. (3) **The `"data"` example from this entry needed more than word boundaries**, and was re-confirmed broken after them: `"data"` is a genuine whole word, so "Is my data encrypted at rest?" tied 1-1 on hit count between `export_reports` and `security_retention`, and Python's stable sort resolved the tie by list position — returning the CSV-export guide for a security question. Fixed two ways: `"data"` dropped from `export_reports` (its other seven keywords cover the topic fully), **and** the sort key is now `(matched keyword count, total matched keyword length)`, so a longer/more specific phrase match (`"at rest"`, `"data security"`) beats a short generic one instead of list order deciding. Verified against that exact question. (4) **The low-confidence path no longer sets `suggest_escalation=True`** — an unanswered question was rendering the same red "Issue Diagnosis & Recommended Escalation" card as a genuine detected incident. (5) **Bonus, pre-existing bug found and fixed in the same matcher**: KB topics are matched *before* `ERROR_TRIGGERS` and return early, so `billing`'s `"payu"` and `"checkout"` keywords made `ERR_PAYU_BILLING_FAILURE` **unreachable** — "payu error on checkout", "my payment failed at checkout" and "checkout crash" all returned the pricing article instead of the payment-failure troubleshooting card. Both keywords removed. - `[x]` **Gap 263 (BE): Chat SQL route misfires on tax-component questions and leaks internal columns/raw Python dicts into results** — opened and closed 2026-08-19, founder-reported from a live chat transcript (Rajesh Steel Corporation invoice, CGST question) during autoloop pre-flight testing. Two distinct defects found in the same conversation:
  1. **Rule 6d (Gap 253's line-item rule) misfired on tax-component terms.** "What's the CGST we paid on the Rajesh Steel invoices?" matched rule 6d's trigger ("a product/service phrase together with a money word") even though CGST/SGST/IGST are never stored as line-item descriptions — this schema tracks only a single combined `tax_amount` per invoice, no separate tax-component split. The generated query searched `item->>'description' LIKE '%cgst%'`, guaranteed zero rows, and the reply said *"I found no Rajesh Steel invoices matching your query"* — false; the invoice existed (confirmed one turn later by a "list all invoices" query), only that one wrong-shaped filter matched nothing.
  2. **`execute_generated_sql()` rendered every selected column verbatim with no hygiene.** A generic "list all the invoices" question selected `batch_id` and `file_path` alongside business columns, and both were dumped straight into the chat window — `file_path` is an internal Azure blob storage URI (`azure://invoices/tenants/<tenant-uuid>/invoices/<file-uuid>.pdf`), exposing internal storage architecture and the tenant UUID on a customer-facing surface. Separately, `items` (a JSONB list-of-dicts, auto-deserialized into native Python objects by psycopg2 even for a raw `text()` query — a DBAPI-level adaptation independent of SQLAlchemy's ORM type system) was rendered via plain `str()`, producing Python's repr (single-quoted keys, `None` instead of `null`) instead of valid JSON.

  **Fixed, `agents/query_agent.py`:**
  1. Both `_LINE_ITEM_RULE_POSTGRES` and `_LINE_ITEM_RULE_SQLITE` gained an explicit exclusion: tax-component terms (CGST/SGST/IGST/VAT/"tax") must not be treated as line-item search targets — the model is steered to answer from `tax_amount` directly instead, and told never to report a zero-row line-item search as "no invoice found" when the invoice-level filters would have matched.
  2. New `_INTERNAL_ONLY_COLUMNS` denylist (`file_path`, `batch_id`) enforced deterministically in `execute_generated_sql()` — stripped from the display table regardless of what the LLM SELECTed, while the full unfiltered column set is still used for Gap 231's invoice-id snapshot harvest (which needs `id`/`invoice_id` even though display hides them). List/dict values (JSONB columns already deserialized by the driver) are now rendered with `json.dumps` instead of `str()`.

  **Architectural note, not addressed in this pass:** this is the third instance in one session of a hygiene rule (Gap 253's "don't select `invoice.id`, it's noise") being written narrowly for the one rule that surfaced it and never generalized — a known, discussed pattern (case-by-case prose rules that don't compose, vs. deterministic code for facts about the schema). The column-denylist fix here follows that direction (code, not prompt) for this specific instance; a broader sweep of the rest of the prompt for the same class of gap (e.g. whether rule 6b/6c have their own untested blind spots) has not been done and is not scoped here.

Full suite: `tests/test_chat_sql_quality.py`, `test_queries.py`, `test_rag.py`, `test_direction_aware_chat.py` — 113/113 passing. **Not yet independently re-verified against a live conversation with the real Azure-connected backend** — the reproduction was against the local unit-test suite only; the same live-verification standard applied to every other gap in this file (real Azure OCR/LLM, not mocked) should be run against this exact CGST question and the "list all invoices" question before this is trusted as fully closed in practice, not just in the test suite.

A match doesn't bypass the LLM — it grounds the SQL prompt with the *specific* term this question actually contains (`tax_term_block`), so the model is handed a fact instead of asked to recall a principle. Extending coverage to a new jurisdiction's tax name is now "add a string, write one test," not "reword a paragraph." **Verified**: `test_detect_tax_component_term_is_deterministic_not_llm_judged` (9 cases incl. a word-boundary negative, "gstreet" must not match), `test_tax_term_block_is_injected_into_the_sql_prompt_when_detected`. 123/123 passing.

Tracker was stale; code already covered this.

  - Who is allowed to set it — likely permission-gated (not every role should be able to mark a vendor bill paid), needs a decision against this repo's existing RBAC roles.
  - Migration for the new column(s); FE button + status display, matching OUTBOUND's existing UI pattern.
  - Once this exists, Gap 267's chat guardrail should be revisited: currently it unconditionally tells the model INBOUND has no payment concept at all — once a real field exists, that instruction needs to change from "always refuse" to "answer from the new field," or chat will keep refusing a question it could now actually answer.
