- `[x]` **Gap 307 (BE/AI): context-drift detection does not exist — a thread can now be reconstructed, but nothing judges whether it drifted** — opened 2026-08-24, **split out of Gap 303 rather than left implicit in it**, because that entry was written as one gap covering two genuinely different pieces of work and closing only the first would have made it look half-done for no stated reason. What Gap 303 built is *reconstruction*: `chat_turn` events carry `session_id`, `turn_index` and `seconds_since_prev_turn`, and `infra/monitoring/chat_thread_sessions.kql` derives session length, turns-per-session and abandonment at a 30-minute idle cutoff. What it did not build, and never claimed to, is a **detector** — anything that looks at turn N in light of turns 1..N-1 and says "the filter narrowed unexpectedly" or "the prior turn's SQL was reused after a topic change". Those are Gap 237 and Gap 276's failure shapes; both are **closed bugs** cited as the failure class, and closing them built no detector. What now exists that a detector could consume, which is strictly more than when Gap 303 was opened: the full per-turn Trace including the real generated SQL and the real tool output for every turn in a session (Gap 302), so a drift check no longer has to re-run retrieval or reason from `ChatMessage` text alone — turn N's SQL and turn N-1's SQL are both queryable side by side from one event stream. Also available: the golden bank's ordered multi-turn scripts (10 follow-up links plus Gap 237's 2-turn capture). **Not built, and the doc's own position is still that it should be scoped down before it is promised** — `feature_20_23_24_ops_workbook.md`'s Multi-turn evaluation tier calls a general multi-turn detector the hardest thing in the feature and recommends fixed 2-3 turn scripts with pinned expectations rather than a general detector. Two shapes are worth costing separately when this is picked up: an **offline** one (a multi-turn tier in the golden bank, which needs no new production code at all) and an **online** one (a signal over live `chat_turn` events, which is where the new Trace content earns its keep but which also means judging live traffic — a product decision of the same class as Gap 304 half 2, not a wiring change). **CLOSED 2026-08-26 — the OFFLINE half is built; the ONLINE half is deliberately NOT, and is recommended below as its own number.** The entry above costed the two shapes separately and asked for them to be picked up separately; this closes the one that “needs no new production code at all”. **Nothing in this change touches a request path, emits a new telemetry event type, adds an Azure resource or edits a bicep file** — it is an eval tier plus one deterministic scorer. **Online half built 2026-08-27 as Gap 324** — a deterministic heuristic riding the live `chat_turn` request path rather than a judge call, so it needed no new deployment surface (sidestepping the exact class of "coded but never deployed" trap Gap 305 named).

  **What was built.** `benchmarks/agent_eval_multiturn.py` (new): **5 scripted conversations, 12 turns, 7 of them drift-scored**, following Wave 3's precedent (its cases are ordinary `GoldenCase`s against the same seeded in-memory SQLite tenant, graded by the same judge, selected by the same `--cases`). The doc's own scoping is honoured literally — `feature_20_23_24_ops_workbook.md` calls a general multi-turn detector the hardest thing in the feature and recommends “fixed 2-3 turn scripts with pinned expectations”: every script is 2 or 3 turns and every expectation is pinned to a seeded row, asserted by test rather than trusted. The five are `drift_subject_switch_vendor` (Gap 276's shape: “now show me DataPipe **instead**” after a Blue Ridge turn), `drift_narrowing_followup_keeps_filter` (Gap 237's shape and its mirror image — “which of those is oldest” must KEEP the over-USD-20,000 filter, because the oldest invoice *overall* is a USD 420.00 one outside it), `drift_referent_moves_with_conversation` (3 turns; “and when is **that one** due” must resolve to turn 2's invoice, not turn 1's — the two carry different due dates on purpose, so a stale referent is a wrong date rather than a matter of opinion), `drift_ambiguous_previous_invoice` (“the previous invoice” said when the prior turn named two), and `drift_scope_stated_once_still_applies` (3 turns; a June-2026 scope stated once, in a turn that asks no question at all, then two questions that never mention it — both with a pinned wrong answer reachable only by dropping it).

  **The scorer is deterministic, not a fourth judge call**, and that is the substantive design decision. `services/agent_eval.py::score_context_drift()` + `DriftExpectation` score *checks passed / checks pinned* over four surfaces kept separate on purpose: `forbidden_sql_terms` (the generated SQL only — Gap 276's predicate survives in the WHERE clause whether or not stale rows reach the prose), `forbidden_terms` (prose *and* SQL), `required_entities` (prose only, one **alias group** per entity) and `forbidden_invoice_numbers` (what the tools actually fetched). Two reasons a judge was rejected: a judge asked “did this drift?” cannot know what the earlier turns established unless it is shown them (more prompt, more variance, more cost per turn), and `services/agent_eval.py` already carries four documented instances of a free-floating judged number systematically under-scoring correct answers. `context_drift_score` is **component-level** like `context`/`orchestration` — recorded and trended, **not** in `decide_pass()`, because folding a new dimension into the pass criterion halfway through a series silently redefines what a pass means. Its stated bias is toward false *passes* (a turn that answers nothing satisfies every forbidden check), the same disclosure `score_orchestration()` makes about itself, and for the same reason: the alternative under-scores correct answers, and a degenerate answer is what faithfulness/relevance/accuracy already catch.

  **The three things that make twelve turns a conversation rather than twelve first turns**, all in `scripts/run_agent_eval.py`: (1) one `session_id` shared across a script (`run_multi_turn_script()`); (2) a `ChatMessage` write-back between turns (`record_turn_messages()`) — necessary because `run_query_agent()` persists nothing, `routers/chat.py::post_chat_message` does, and the two functions drift actually happens in (`get_chat_history()`, and Gap 237's own `get_prior_turn_sql()`, which filters on `generated_sql IS NOT NULL`) read exactly those rows — without it every drift check would pass vacuously; (3) its own summary bucket `default-multiturn` (`services/benchmark_artifacts.py::MULTI_TURN_PATH`), so the 35-case `default` series keeps the exact population every historical figure in the docs was computed over. `--no-multi-turn` skips the tier; otherwise it runs on the nightly path the way every other tier does, with no bicep and no job-argv change. The tier's `agent_eval_summary` event rides the **existing** per-path mechanism (built for `default`/`sage`), and `context_drift_score` rides `agent_eval_run`'s `**extra_attributes` exactly as Track 2's helpfulness/completeness/tone already do — no new event type, and no `AgentEvalRun` column or migration (the value also lands in `notes`, like `judge_mode`).

  **Nightly review wiring.** `evaluate_ai_improvement()` reads the drift bucket by its own key (`_multi_turn_stats()`, never averaged into the single-turn numbers) and raises a `context_drift` finding graded on **`d3-context`'s existing band** rather than a new pair of numbers — drift *is* a retrieval failure, and every threshold in that module is a live tile's, pinned by a test that parses both workbook JSONs. There is no drift tile today and adding one is a workbook deploy, out of scope here; inventing an uncalibrated `CONTEXT_DRIFT_RED` would have been the first band in that file with no tile behind it. It is exempt from the n=20 sample guard, and that is stated in code: the tier is a fixed, exhaustive, deterministic script set run identically every night, so there is no sampling error for the guard to protect against and applying it would disable the tier permanently. `_agent_eval_stats()` now also excludes the drift bucket from its path *choice*, so a `--cases <script>` run cannot get its 12 deliberately harder turns graded against the 35-case bank's bands.

  **Real evidence, not “should work” — two live runs against the configured Azure `gpt-5-mini`, real agent and real judge, `--no-persist --no-mirror`.** **Run A**, all 5 scripts: **12/12 turns ran, 0 errors**, `$0.005`/turn, and the `default-multiturn` bucket reported `pass_rate 0.333`, `faithfulness_mean 0.806`, `accuracy_mean 0.742` and **`context_drift_mean 0.943` over 7 scored turns**. Six of the seven scored 1.00, and the generated SQL proves it was not luck: the June-2026 scope survived **two** later turns (`invoice_date >= DATE('2026-06-01') AND invoice_date <= DATE('2026-06-30')` present in both turn 2's and turn 3's SQL, two and three turns after it was stated), and `currency = 'USD' AND grand_total > 20000` survived the “which of those is oldest” follow-up. **The seventh scored 0.60 — and it was the harness's fault, which is the whole point of having run it.** `drift_ambiguous_previous_invoice` turn 2 answered “Do you mean the invoice dated 2026-06-27 (SEP-4410) or 2026-06-30 (DPS-9981)? SEP-4410 tax = USD 2,236.00; DPS-9981 tax = USD 3,384.00” — the exact clarifying question that case exists to reward, with SQL filtering on both vendors — and was marked drifted because the check demanded the vendor *names* while the answer used the invoice *numbers*. That is precisely the under-scoring-correct-answers trap this repo has four prior instances of, found on the first live run rather than in production: `required_terms` was replaced by `required_entities` (alias groups — one check per entity, satisfied by any of its stable surface forms), and that exact answer text is now a regression test. **Run B**, the same script re-run after the fix, is the check firing on a genuine failure: the model **silently** resolved “the previous invoice” to `DPS-9981` without saying which of the two it had picked — `context_drift 0.80` with the note “the subject under discussion went missing: StratEdge/SEP-4410”, and the independent accuracy judge scored the same turn `0.0`. False positive removed, true positive kept.

  **Tests: 43 new in `tests/test_agent_eval_multiturn.py`**, plus 9 in `test_ops_recommendation.py` and 1 in `test_benchmark_artifacts.py`. They pin the scorer's mechanics and — more usefully — the scripts' well-formedness against the real fixture: every pinned invoice number is seeded, every pinned term is a string the fixture can actually produce, no pinned term is a money figure (formatting varies by route and a missed forbidden match reads as “no drift”), every alias group resolves to exactly one seeded invoice, no term is both required and forbidden on the same turn, every required entity appears in its own reference answer, every forbidden term is explained by that answer, no first turn carries a drift expectation and every later turn does. The three fixture facts the wrong answers depend on are asserted too (oldest-overall is outside the >20k set; largest-overall is outside June; the only freight line is outside June) — a future fixture edit that quietly makes a drift case undiscriminating fails a test instead of going green. **339 tests pass across the six affected files** (`test_agent_eval_multiturn` 43, `test_ops_recommendation` 83, `test_benchmark_artifacts` 40, `test_run_agent_eval_cli` 19, `test_agent_eval` 97, `test_telemetry` 60); the full suite is deliberately **not** claimed here — it is reserved for a track-boundary checkpoint. Two existing tests changed and both are worth stating: one in `test_benchmark_artifacts.py` was re-anchored from “all nine dimensions are on the event” to “every dimension the run actually *scored* is on the event”, because `context_drift` is legitimately absent from a `default`-bucket event and demanding otherwise would demand a 0.0 for a dimension never measured; and `_run_main()` in `test_run_agent_eval_cli.py` now stubs the tier out for the same reason it already stubs `CASES` — without it a CLI unit test makes twelve real model calls, found by running it.

  **NOT closed by this, and it needs its own number: the ONLINE judge — recommended as `Gap 321`.** A live signal over production `chat_turn` events is explicitly out of scope here and is **not** part of this closure. It is the half the entry above describes as “where the new Trace content earns its keep but which also means judging live traffic — a product decision of the same class as Gap 304 half 2, not a wiring change”, and that assessment is unchanged. **321 is the next free number in this tracker** (320 is the current maximum). What it would inherit from this gap and should not rebuild: the definition of drift, the four-surface check shape, and `services/online_eval_signals.py`'s existing signal/threshold/`online_eval_signal` plumbing. What it must decide, and what this gap deliberately does not: whether production turns may be judged at all and at what sampling rate; what plays the part of a pinned expectation when there is no golden script (the hard problem — nothing tells a live detector what turn N *should* have been about); and what it costs per judged turn.

- `[x]` **Gap 296 (BE): a hallucinated chat route was answered conversationally instead of being caught.** `QueryRoutingSchema.route` (`agents/query_agent.py`) was typed `str` with a description merely *asking* for `RAG`/`SQL`/`CHAT`, so the emitted JSON schema carried no `enum` and nothing constrained the model's output. Because `run_query_agent()` dispatches `if SQL / elif RAG / else: # CHAT`, **any** unrecognised value fell through to the conversational branch: the user got a chatty answer, no retrieval ran, and nothing recorded that routing had failed. Found 2026-08-23 by a live smoke test of the corrected `OLLAMA_MODEL` default (`llama3.2:latest`), which returned syntactically valid structured output with an invented `route` — schema-valid and semantically wrong. Fixed by typing the field `Literal["RAG", "SQL", "CHAT"]` (a real `enum` the provider constrains generation against) plus a `mode="before"` validator that strips/upper-cases, so the case-tolerance the old `result.route.upper()` provided is preserved exactly; an out-of-vocabulary value now raises and `classify_query()`'s existing `except` falls back to RAG, which does retrieve. **Azure regression evidence, measured before and after rather than asserted**: 30/30 live gpt-5-mini classifications parsed with 0 validation errors in both states, and a same-process old-schema-vs-new-schema A/B over 96 live calls had 0 errors in either arm and identical routes on every unambiguous question. Qualification stated rather than buried: on *genuinely ambiguous* questions the sampled distribution does shift (reproducibly for one question, and in the opposite direction for another), but the old typing was a coin flip on exactly those questions, so neither arm is a correct baseline there. **The premise is unverified** — that the enum fixes non-Azure models could not be tested, no Ollama server was running.

- `[x]` **The two judge failure modes Phase 3 left open are fixed** — 2026-08-21, later the same day, both as rubric corrections rather than per-question special cases, and both diagnosed from the persisted output of the run that exhibited them (`tests/agent_eval_output.json`) rather than guessed at. **(3) A correct "no records found" scored 0.00 faithfulness because the judge was never shown the query.** The evidence handed to it was the whole of `"DATABASE RESULTS:\nNo records found matching the query criteria."` while the claims under judgement named *Nonexistent Holdings* and *last quarter* — neither of which appears anywhere in that evidence, so the 0/2 verdict was correct on what it was given. The verdict prompt's own rule 5 already anticipated this ("supported when the context shows that query was the one executed") but its precondition could never be met. Fixed by threading `executed_queries` (SQL + every tool call with its arguments) through `score_faithfulness()`/`score_answer()` and `scripts/run_agent_eval.py`, and by replacing the bolted-on empty-result carve-out with a per-claim `claim_type` (`positive_fact`/`absence`/`query_scope`/`non_factual`) the judge must assign *before* deciding, with the evidence standard stated per type; `non_factual` claims now leave the denominator instead of costing score. **(4) The same correct out-of-scope refusal scored 1.0 on SAGE and 0.0 on the default path** because every numeric anchor in the relevance rubric was phrased as *"answers what was asked"* — which a refusal by construction does not — so the three carve-outs appended after them were fighting the rubric they were attached to. Fixed by making the judge classify an `answer_kind` first, with the score fixed **in code** (`RELEVANCE_KIND_SCORES`) for the kinds whose relevance is definitional (`no_results_report`/`out_of_scope_refusal`/`capability_or_greeting` → 1.0, `off_topic` → 0.0) and judged only for `direct_answer`/`clarifying_question`. Tests are pinned to the **real answer texts from the failing run**, and the refusal test feeds in the actual 0.0-vs-1.0 divergence to assert it no longer propagates. `tests/test_agent_eval.py` 19 → 55 passed. **Not re-run against a live model**: the fixes change scoring, so pre-fix and post-fix figures are not comparable and post-fix numbers do not exist yet.
- `[x]` **Component-level scoring** — `context_score` / `orchestration_score` / `persona_score` on `AgentEvalRun` + alembic `c4a91e77b208` (chained onto `b5d2c8a41f30`, confirmed the real single head by running `alembic heads` first, single head re-verified after; three nullable floats, no server default, so every existing row reads as "not scored" and never as 0.0). Three genuinely different mechanisms, not one check run three times: **context** is a deterministic F1 of fetched invoice ids against the golden case's known-correct set (no judge — a case whose correct retrieval is *nothing* scores 1.0 for fetching nothing, which is Gap 224's shape); **orchestration** is mechanical figure traceability (every number in the answer must appear in a tool result or be arithmetic over ones that do — also no judge); **persona** is the one LLM-judged component, with an explicit `applicable=false` escape. Mirrored onto the `agent_eval_run` custom event and given **three separate trend lines** in the workbook, per the feature's own "not one blended average" instruction. **Additive and inert — they do not feed the pass decision** (folding them in would redefine what a pass means halfway through a trend series). **One honest limitation, in the code, the doc and the workbook panel**: there is no dedicated domain-knowledge golden set in this repo, so persona is scored against the general sample with a persona-focused rubric and returns NULL on most turns — read `persona_scored_turns` before reading `persona`. Writing that bank is still outstanding. A second under-scoring path was found by running the orchestration check against the 2026-08-21 round's real output (a correct answer's derived `USD 20.00` discrepancy marked untraceable) and fixed by allowing a second arithmetic hop restricted to already-grounded figures.

  **The single combined tabbed workbook was retired and split into 9 standalone workbooks — 2026-08-23.** Reason: Azure lets you pin a whole workbook or an individual visual to a Dashboard, but a pinned tile does not evaluate the source workbook's own `conditionalVisibility`/`SelectedTab` tab logic, so a single tab could never be reliably pinned out of the combined file. `infra/monitoring/ai_control_tower.workbook.json` (the tab bar + 8 `SelectedTab`-gated groups) was deleted; in its place are 9 standalone JSON files in the same folder (`ai_control_tower_summary.workbook.json` plus one per former tab: `_cost`, `_latency`, `_quality`, `_component_quality`, `_online_signals`, `_golden_bank`, `_health`, `_documentation`), each carrying its own copy of the shared `TimeRange`/`Subscription`/`Tenant` parameter block (`type: 9`) so every KQL query's `{Tenant}` substitution and `timeContextFromParameter` still resolve standalone. Each non-Summary file is its former tab's `items` array unwrapped (group wrapper and `conditionalVisibility` dropped, content otherwise untouched); the Summary file preserves the old overview group's hidden-query merge mechanism (`nevershow` `conditionalVisibility` on the two source steps, `queryType: 7` union feeding the `tiles` step) byte-for-byte. Per later founder direction the same session, Summary also **embeds the full Documentation content as a collapsed `type: 12` group** (`loadButtonText: "Show full documentation"`, `expandable: true`, `expanded: false` — the same pattern as the pre-existing "Cost by tool" collapsible section) so pinning Summary's tiles to a Dashboard and clicking through reaches Documentation with no extra navigation, rather than a dead end at just the 7 tiles; the embedded copy and the standalone `_documentation` file are asserted textually identical so they cannot drift apart. New `infra/monitoring/ai_control_tower_workbooks.bicep` deploys all 9 as `Microsoft.Insights/workbooks@2022-04-01` resources (`serializedData` via `loadTextContent()` per file, `appi-invoicellm-dev` referenced as `existing`, not routed through `08-apps.bicep`/`params.dev.json` — same narrow-standalone-deploy rationale as `agent-eval-job-only.bicep`). `az bicep build` passed; `az deployment group what-if` against `rg-invoice-llm-dev` returned a clean **9 to create, 0 to modify, 0 to delete**. **Not yet deployed** — `az deployment group create` was deliberately not run, pending founder go-ahead.

- `[x]` **Gap 309 (BE/AI): `extraction_benchmark_run` telemetry was silently discarded by
  `logging`'s own level check — the exporter was attached correctly and never received a
  single record** — opened and fixed 2026-08-24, **found live in the same deployed run as Gap
  308**. Both of that execution's tracks printed a success line; only Track 2's
  `agent_eval_summary` was actually findable in `customEvents`. Track 1's stdout said
  `mirror [nightly] -> Application Insights + stdout: 1 telemetry event(s)` and **nothing
  arrived, on that run or any earlier one.** Root cause is one line before the exporter or the
  flush could matter: `telemetry._emit_event()` calls `logger.info(...)` on
  `invoice_be_telemetry`, and `configure_azure_monitor()` **adds a handler without ever
  setting a level** (verified against the installed distro — `azure/monitor/opentelemetry/
  _configure.py` only does `getLogger(logger_name).addHandler(handler)`). The logger therefore
  sits at `NOTSET`, inherits root's `WARNING` in a bare `python scripts/...` process, and
  `Logger.isEnabledFor(INFO)` is **False** — the record is dropped inside `logging` before any
  handler, Azure Monitor's included, is consulted. The reassuring stdout line is
  `MirrorResult.describe()` counting emitter *calls*. Exactly the silent-no-op class Gap 292
  named, one level lower down. **Why Track 2 was unaffected, which is what made this hard to
  see:** `scripts/run_agent_eval.py::_counting_llm_calls()` attaches its per-turn
  `_LlmCallCounter` to both event loggers and calls `lg.setLevel(logging.INFO)` to do it, and
  its `finally` removes the handler but never restores the level — so Track 2 has been carried
  the whole time by a side effect of an unrelated measurement helper firing on its first turn.
  `scripts/sweep_azure_cost.py` and `scripts/ops_digest_job.py` are covered by a different
  accident: both call `utils.logging_config.setup_structured_logging()`, which sets the
  **root** logger to INFO. `scripts/run_extraction_benchmark.py` does neither and was the only
  one of the four with nothing holding the level up. **Consequence beyond the mirror event:**
  every per-call `llm_agent_call` from a Track 1 `--mode live` run was being dropped the same
  way, so Gap 304 half (1)'s "the run's own per-call events now export, tagged `golden`" was
  true of Track 2 only. **Fix:** `_enable_event_logger_level()` (new,
  `services/benchmark_artifacts.py`), called first thing in `configure_run_telemetry()` — the
  one function both benchmark scripts already call to make telemetry work in a standalone
  process. Raises both names in `telemetry._EVENT_LOGGER_NAMES` to INFO, leaves a level the
  caller deliberately set *lower* (DEBUG) alone, and runs on the no-connection-string path too
  so a stdout-only run produces the structured console line the module docstring promises.
  **Why the 1400-test suite never caught this:** every existing assertion on these events
  either uses `caplog.at_level(logging.INFO)` (which raises the level itself) or patches
  `telemetry._emit_event` outright (so the level check never runs). The 5 new tests avoid both
  — 4 in `tests/test_benchmark_artifacts.py` (including one pinning the *premise*: at default
  levels an INFO event reaches no handler at all) and 1 end-to-end in
  `tests/test_run_extraction_benchmark_cli.py` driving the real `main()` with a recording
  handler attached exactly where the distro attaches its own. Both fail without the fix,
  verified by reverting it.

  anything (the previously-recorded `1414 passed / 7 failed` was stale — other workstreams

- **Real product defect surfaced by the Phase 3 run, recorded here rather than lost in a JSON file** — 2026-08-21. Asked *"whats the CGST we paid to Rajesh Steel"* against a fixture holding one combined `tax_amount` of INR 18,000.00 and no per-component breakdown, the **current default chat path** answered *"The CGST recorded for Rajesh Steel is INR 18,000.00"* — relabelling the combined tax as CGST. That is Gaps 263/264's failure mode, live, reproduced against the real model. SAGE Phase 2 answered the same question correctly (*"This schema does not store per-tax-type lines…the combined tax total…is ₹18,000"*). Not opened as a new Gap: it is the same class Feature 21 exists to fix structurally, and Gap 285's entry already records the decision not to patch this one field at a time. Evidence: `tests/agent_eval_output.json`, case `rajesh_steel_cgst`. **Closed by Gap 310 (below, 2026-08-25)** — and not in the way this entry expected: rather than shipping SAGE, Gap 310 retrofitted SAGE's core full-record fetch onto the default path, so the fix landed on the cheap route and SAGE's Phase 3 remains gated. The `rajesh_steel_cgst` golden case has been rewritten accordingly — it now expects the real INR 9,000.00 CGST rather than the decline SAGE Phase 2 gave, because the decline was never true of the *data*, only of the prompt.

- `[x]` **Gap 310 (BE/AI): the default chat route answered detail questions from a hand-typed 19-column schema block while the real `Invoice` row had long since outgrown it — the identified invoice's whole record now reaches the answering step** — 2026-08-25. **The failure class, not one field.** `taxes` (the itemized per-component tax rows, each with its own `tax_type`/`rate_percent`/`amount`), `subtotal`, `tax_ids`, `discounts`, `deductions`, `payment_instructions`, `references`, `compliance_metadata` and `field_confidence` are all real columns on `Invoice`, all populated by `queue_worker/handlers.py`, and **none was visible to the SQL route at all** — schema drift between a live model and a prompt maintained by hand. Measured live 2026-08-21 (the "Real product defect surfaced by the Phase 3 run" entry above): *"whats the CGST we paid to Rajesh Steel"* → *"The CGST recorded for Rajesh Steel is INR 18,000.00"*, relabelling the combined `tax_amount` as CGST while the invoice's own `taxes` held CGST 9% INR 9,000.00 + SGST 9% INR 9,000.00. **Fix**: `agents/query_agent.py::_full_record_block_for(invoice_ids, tenant_id, db_session)` calls `query_tools.get_full_record(..., include_document_pages=False)` (new keyword, added for this — SAGE keeps the default, so its behaviour is byte-identical) and interpolates the rendered record into the SQL route's summary prompt as `{db_result}{full_record_block}`. **Four decisions, each of them the point rather than an implementation detail**: (1) **generic, never keyword-gated** — it fires on every turn that identified at least one invoice, whatever was asked. A tax-keyword gate was built and then explicitly rejected on founder correction mid-run (2026-08-24): a keyword gate is the same failure mode this route already has two named instances of (rule 6d's tax-component miss, Gap 264's fixed term list), and "which discounts were applied" / "what's the vendor's GSTIN" / "what's the subtotal before tax" are the same gap wearing different words. (2) **Deterministic, no extra LLM round-trip** — binding a `get_invoice_full_record` tool to the summary model would cost a whole additional generation per turn to decide a `db_session.get()` on a primary key. (3) **Bounded on both axes**, so it cannot inherit SAGE's unmeasured cost profile: `MAX_FULL_RECORD_INVOICES = 3` (a turn that identified 40 rows is an aggregate or a listing, where 40 complete records would be both useless and the largest single thing in the prompt) and `MAX_FULL_RECORD_BLOCK_CHARS = 12_000`; the surplus is **disclosed in the block** with its count, not silently dropped, the same honesty rule `columns_omitted`/`pages_omitted` follow — with one deliberate exception, the first record renders however large, because an empty block plus "everything was held back" is strictly worse than a long one. No Chroma call and no page dump (`include_document_pages=False`; Feature 21's B4 run measured a page dump at up to 16,010 tokens on an 11-page invoice), since this route already has its own document channel in the RAG branch. (4) **Fail-soft and tenant-safe** — any failure logs, rolls back and returns `""`, leaving the turn exactly the results table it had before; cross-tenant ids come back `not_found` from `get_full_record` itself, never a distinguishable error, which is the second of two independent checks since the ids came from a query `execute_generated_sql`'s Safety Check 3 already forced to be tenant-scoped. **Two ordering/consistency changes came with it**: the Gap 231 companion-query id harvest moved **above** the summary-prompt construction (it decides which invoices the turn is about; running it after would have left the block permanently empty for exactly the single-invoice detail questions it exists for, since rules 6d/11 forbid selecting `id`), and the block is appended to `judge_context_parts` (Gap 304 half 2 — otherwise a correct CGST figure read off `taxes` scores unfaithful purely because the judge saw a narrower evidence set than the model did). **The tax-term note was corrected, not removed**: `_tax_term_block_for()` fires on the same detection but no longer ends *"This schema has no breakdown by tax type; select tax_amount directly"* — true when Gap 263 wrote it, false ever since extraction began populating `taxes`, and a prompt asserting a capability gap the product no longer has instructs the model to decline an answerable question. **Benchmark fixtures moved with the product**: `benchmarks/sage_seed_fixtures.py`'s Rajesh Steel row seeds the real CGST/SGST breakdown (9% + 9% summing to the INR 18,000.00 already in `tax_amount`, on an INR 100,000.00 subtotal — the two representations agree, or the golden case would be ungradeable), with `taxes` defaulted to `"[]"` for the other rows; `benchmarks/agent_eval_golden_sample.py`'s `rajesh_steel_cgst` was rewritten from expecting a **decline** to expecting **INR 9,000.00**, its rubric still guarding the original live failure (the figures must be read, never derived by halving the total); `benchmarks/region_seed_fixtures.py`'s "CGST/SGST questions cannot be ported, the schema has no tax-component column" rationale is struck through rather than deleted, because it was wrong in an instructive way — there was never a schema limitation, only a prompt one, and adding a regional CGST case is now a fixture edit plus a `GoldenCase` with no product change behind it. **Verified**: 8 tests in `tests/test_chat_sql_quality.py` (`-k full_record`) covering all five properties — the real breakdown plus `subtotal`/`tax_ids` reach the summary prompt *and* the judge evidence; a question with no tax word in it (`detect_tax_component_term()` → `None`) gets the identical record, which is what proves the mechanism is not keyword-gated; another tenant's row yields nothing directly, nothing when mixed with a legitimate id, and nothing through the whole route; a raising `get_full_record` leaves the answer and results table intact; **both** bounds hold (count bound, character budget with the held-back count disclosed, and the single-oversized-record exception); and a turn that identified nothing is byte-identical to its pre-Gap-310 behaviour. Full `pytest tests/test_*.py -p no:randomly` before **1381 passed / 3 failed / 7 skipped**, after **1383 passed / 3 failed / 7 skipped** (+2, the new character-budget tests), the **same 3 pre-existing failures** as Gap 311's run (2x `test_connectors.py` needing a local Redis, 1x `test_rag.py` calling `post_chat_message()` without `background_tasks`). `ruff check` clean on all six touched/related files. **Deliberately still open**: these are mocked unit tests and assert mechanics only — the behavioural evidence is the `rajesh_steel_cgst` golden case under a live-model `scripts/run_agent_eval.py` run, which has **not** been re-run since the rewrite, so the case's new expectation is not yet backed by a measured pass. That live result is also the blocking condition on SAGE Phase 3 (Feature 21 entry above). Design in `docs/feature_6_rag.md`, "Recent Fix (Aug 24–25, 2026) — Gap 310".

- `[x]` **Gap 313 (BE/AI): Feature 6's four chat prompts each carried their own persona and their own copy of the currency rule, and none of them carried any tax-domain knowledge at all — one shared persona block now opens all four, derived from SAGE's** — 2026-08-25. **The asymmetry, not a defect in any one prompt.** The default chat route (`agents/query_agent.py`, the only route any real tenant is on, since `ENABLE_AGENTIC_SAGE` is off) had **four separately hand-written system prompts** — SQL generation (`build_sql_system_prompt()`), the SQL summary prompt built inline in `run_query_agent()`, the RAG prompt and the CHAT prompt. Each opened with its own one-line persona (*"You are a database SQL query expert"* / *"You are an assistant answering questions about invoice documents"* / *"You are a helpful assistant for an AI Invoice Processing platform"*) and each restated the same currency rule in its own words — three of them verbatim-identical, which is duplication with nothing enforcing that the copies stay equal. What **none** of them had was domain knowledge: nothing on this route told the model that CGST always equals SGST on an intra-state invoice, that an IGST-only invoice is inter-state rather than missing a component, that `tax_amount = 0` under RCM is CORRECT rather than an extraction gap, that GSTIN/VAT number/EIN are the same concept in three jurisdictions, that IRN/e-Way Bill/Peppol ID are compliance identifiers rather than tax amounts, that US sales tax and Indian GST mean different things by *"how much tax did we pay"*, that a vendor's own name is as good a category signal as a tag, or that a zero total is never a confident answer. Feature 21 had written every one of those as `agents/sage_prompts.py::PERSONA_BLOCK` and shared it between SAGE's planner and synthesis prompts — but SAGE is off by default, **so the route that actually answers users was the one without it**. **Fix**: `agents/query_agent.py::CHAT_PERSONA_BLOCK`, built once at import by `_build_chat_persona_block()` and prepended to all four prompts. **Derived from `PERSONA_BLOCK`, not copied** — the constant is imported and the tax/category/honesty text is byte-identical to SAGE's, so a rule added there reaches all four of these prompts with no edit here; a second copy of a persona is a persona that disagrees with itself as soon as one copy is edited, which is the same argument `sage_prompts.py` already makes for sharing one block between its own two prompts. The import is safe at module scope: `sage_prompts.py` is pure text plus a `models.Invoice` reflection, and `test_flag_off_never_imports_the_orchestrator_module` forbids `sage_orchestrator`/`query_tools` there, not the prompt text. **The opener needed no change** — `feature_6_rag.md`'s own title is "Conversational RAG & Thread Management — **SAGE Agent**", so *"You are SAGE, a financial-documents assistant…"* is correct on this path too. **Exactly two adaptations**, each because the sentence is *false* here rather than merely awkward: (1) the closing *"You answer only from what your tools actually returned"* — this route has no tools — restated by `_CHAT_GROUNDING_BLOCK` in terms of what it really puts in front of the model ("the query results, document context and invoice records given to you below"), which also agrees with rule 8a's existing "the conversation history is not a data source"; (2) the category section's promise that an ambiguous name match *"has already been routed to a clarifying question before you see it"*, true of the orchestrator (`ask_clarifying_question` is one of its tools) and false here, where it would have told the model that the ambiguity in front of it could not exist — replaced with "report every candidate the name matched and say it matched more than one". `_CHAT_GROUNDING_BLOCK` also carries the one Feature 6 rule `PERSONA_BLOCK` has no equivalent of: **currency presentation** (SAGE's persona forbids summing across currencies but never says which symbol to print), now stated once instead of three times. **Nothing route-specific was lost.** The SQL prompt keeps its schema block and all eleven rules verbatim — including rule 7 (*also* `SELECT` the `currency` column), which merely shared the "CRITICAL CURRENCY RULE" label with the presentation rule and is different SQL mechanics; the summary prompt keeps the line-item template, the reconciliation-mismatch exception and "YOU compute this total, not the database"; the RAG prompt keeps its chunk context and 1–3 sentence directive; the CHAT prompt keeps its SCOPE boundary against writing arbitrary code. `_tax_term_block_for()`/`_payment_status_block_for()` are untouched. Each prompt lost exactly one line: its own persona opener, or its own copy of the currency sentence. **Verified**: 5 new tests in `tests/test_chat_sql_quality.py` (`-k persona`) — one asserting the derivation against `sage_prompts.PERSONA_BLOCK` itself (sections and four distinctive sentences present verbatim; `"your tools"`/`"clarifying question"` present in SAGE's block and **absent** from this one, so a future upstream rewording fails in CI rather than silently reinstating agent-only framing), and four running the real route with the LLM mocked to assert the block reached each of the four prompts at its actual call site, fingerprinted on *"Peppol ID is an e-invoicing network address"* plus a second sentence from a different section, present **once** not twice, with the old per-prompt currency sentence gone and each prompt's own mechanics intact. **`tests/fixtures/query_agent_flag_off_parity.json` regenerated deliberately** (it compares eight scripted turns' prompts byte-for-byte): diffed field by field first — `result` **byte-identical on all eight cases** (same answers, same generated SQL, same citations), the only diffs being the intended one-line-out / one-block-in substitution in every prompt. Reasoning recorded in `tests/agentic_sage_parity_cases.py`'s regeneration log, per that file's own rule. `pytest tests/test_agentic_sage.py` **41 passed**; `pytest tests/test_chat_sql_quality.py` 79 → **84 passed / 5 skipped**. Full `pytest tests/test_*.py -p no:randomly` before **1383 passed / 3 failed / 7 skipped**, after ****1388 passed / 3 failed / 7 skipped** (+5, exactly the new persona tests)** — the same 3 pre-existing failures (2x `test_connectors.py` needing a local Redis, 1x `test_rag.py::test_process_crash_during_agent_leaves_no_orphan_user_message` calling `post_chat_message()` without `background_tasks`, reproduced unchanged here). `ruff check` clean on all three touched files. **Deliberately out of scope**: `agents/sage_prompts.py` and `agents/sage_orchestrator.py` are unchanged and SAGE stays fully functional — this only *reads* from them. - `[x]` **Gap 315 (BE/AI): Feature 6's SQL-summary step asked the LLM to do the arithmetic — Gap 269's root cause, left open when Gap 269 was closed at the formatting level — the totals are now computed in Python before the model is invoked** — 2026-08-25. **Two shipped fixes had between them moved the arithmetic from the database to the LLM and stopped there.** Gap 273 correctly removed SQL-side aggregation for rule 6d (letting one query both *find* and *sum/group* the matching lines was the repeated source of wrong answers — the wrong column summed, the wrong thing grouped), but replaced it with an *instruction*: *"YOU compute this total, not the database … Add the `line_amount` values yourself, per currency, from the rows actually listed above — carefully; this is real arithmetic on real numbers, not decoration."* Gap 269 had already measured what that produces: live 2026-08-19 (US tenant test, Q4/Q10) the model printed *"5000.00 units × USD 0.08 = USD 420.00"* — a false equation, since 5000 × 0.08 is 400.00 and 420.00 was the *stored* amount, i.e. a row that genuinely reconciles two ways with one figure taken from each side. **Gap 269 was closed at the formatting level** (a prose rule about when not to print an "="), so the root cause — LLM-performed arithmetic — survived its own fix. CONVENTIONS.md hard rule 3 is explicit that a check deciding correctness must be deterministic code, and a total is exactly that. **Fix**: `agents/query_agent.py::_computed_figures_block_for(db_result)` parses the turn's own results table and runs `query_tools.compute()` over it — the same LLM-free function SAGE uses, **imported, not reimplemented** — interpolating the figures into the summary prompt as `{db_result}{computed_figures_block}{full_record_block}`. **Two table shapes, both taken from `sage_orchestrator._grounded_arithmetic()`**: (a) rule 6d's line-item table (`line_qty`/`line_unit_price`/`line_amount`) → `reconcile_line_items` per row, so the stored amount, the amount `quantity × unit_price` actually computes to, and the difference are all present and labelled before the model runs; plus a per-currency total of the line amounts; plus **one subtotal per `vendor_name`** when the rows span more than one vendor (`MAX_COMPUTED_VENDOR_GROUPS = 10`) — not a bonus, since the prompt asks for that breakdown by name and without it the "don't do arithmetic" instruction would push the model straight back into arithmetic for that one case; (b) any other table with **more than one** row → a per-currency `sum_by_currency` of each money column, classified by `is_summable_money_column()` (`avg_grand_total` and `line_qty` are never summed — a header is the only thing that says what a number *means*). Single-row tables are skipped: the query already aggregated, and "summing" one row would label its own figure as a total this block computed. **The instruction swaps per turn**: `_DETERMINISTIC_TOTALS_INSTRUCTION` when figures were computed, `_LLM_TOTALS_INSTRUCTION` when not — and the fallback is the pre-Gap-315 wording **verbatim**, which is why a turn with nothing to compute renders a byte-identical prompt and **`tests/fixtures/query_agent_flag_off_parity.json` needed no regeneration** (all eight scripted cases return `NO_RECORDS_FOUND`, so all eight take the fallback; the golden passed untouched, which is the parity evidence for this change). **Disclosed in the prompt, deliberately not a runtime correction** — same shape as Gap 310's full-record block: a validate-then-correct pass would leave the model's own arithmetic on the critical path and then have to decide what to do with an answer whose number is wrong but whose sentences are built around it. The mismatch rule ("state both figures and the difference, never an 'x = y' equation") lives in the block's **header**, once, never beside the figure it applies to — a live SAGE run had gpt-5-mini copy exactly such a parenthetical straight into a user's answer. **Fail-soft on every axis**: an unreadable table, a money column with one unparseable cell, a `compute()` returning `error`, or any exception yields `""` and the old instruction — degraded to pre-Gap-315 behaviour, never a failed turn; and a `compute()` error drops **that figure only**, never a partial one (a total built from most of the rows is a wrong number that looks like a right one). The block is appended to `judge_context_parts` (Gap 304 half 2) — a total the model was told to quote is part of the evidence its answer is grounded in. **One boundary narrowed deliberately**: `compute` joins `get_full_record` as a named exception in the two tests that police the SAGE boundary (`test_agentic_sage.py::test_the_orchestrator_is_reachable_only_through_the_settings_flag`, `test_query_tools.py::test_no_orchestration_tool_is_wired_into_the_live_chat_pipeline`), on the identical criterion Gap 310 used — no LLM call, no SQL generation, no orchestration decision; the other four tools stay reachable only behind `ENABLE_AGENTIC_SAGE`, and the module-scope import ban on `query_tools` is unchanged (the import is inside the calling function, as Gap 310's is). **Verified**: 7 new tests in `tests/test_chat_sql_quality.py` (`-k "computed or line_item_totals or aggregated or compute_error"`) — the load-bearing one replays Gap 269's own row (5000.00 × 0.08 stored as 420.00) beside a line that does reconcile and asserts the prompt carries `"…USD 420.00 stated, 5000 x USD 0.08 computes to USD 400.00 -- USD 20.00 mismatch"`, the deterministic total `USD 720.00`, the plain `=` form for the reconciling line only, **no** `"5000 x USD 0.08 = USD 420.00"` anywhere, the swapped instruction (old wording gone), the mismatch rule positioned above the figures, and the figures present in the judge evidence; the rest cover the per-vendor/per-currency split (no blended `750.00`), the non-line-item money-column shape, the single-already-aggregated-row skip, five nothing-to-compute cases, the fail-soft path (a raising `compute` leaves answer, results table and original instruction intact), and a `compute()` error dropping only its own figure. `pytest tests/test_chat_sql_quality.py tests/test_query_tools.py tests/test_agentic_sage.py` **221 passed / 5 skipped**. Full `pytest tests/test_*.py -q` before **1388 passed / 3 failed / 7 skipped** (measured on this same tree with the 7 new tests `--deselect`ed, and equal to Gap 313's recorded after-count), after **1395 passed / 3 failed / 7 skipped** (+7, exactly the new tests) — the **same 3 pre-existing failures** (2x `test_connectors.py` needing a local Redis, 1x `test_rag.py::test_process_crash_during_agent_leaves_no_orphan_user_message` calling `post_chat_message()` without `background_tasks`). `ruff check` clean on `agents/query_agent.py` and `tests/test_chat_sql_quality.py`; the two F401s ruff reports in `tests/test_agentic_sage.py` / `tests/test_query_tools.py` are **pre-existing**, confirmed by running ruff against each file's `HEAD` version, and were left alone rather than swept in. **Deliberately out of scope**: `agents/query_tools.py` and `agents/sage_orchestrator.py` are unchanged — this only *reads* from them; `ENABLE_AGENTIC_SAGE` is untouched. **Known follow-on, stated not hidden**: Feature 6 now depends on two functions inside `query_tools.py` (`get_full_record` from Gap 310, `compute` from here), so whatever removes or relocates SAGE's code has to rehome both rather than delete them. Mocked unit tests assert mechanics — but here the mechanics *are* the fix, since the arithmetic no longer depends on model behaviour at all; what a live run would still show is whether the model quotes the given figures rather than restating them. Design in `docs/feature_6_rag.md`, "Recent Fix (Aug 25, 2026) — Gap 315".

- `[x]` **Gap 316 (BE/AI): Feature 21's SAGE orchestrator deleted — a real live-tenant head-to-head showed it cost +87% per turn and +90% median latency to answer nothing the default path got wrong, and leaked internal tool caveats to users on 5 of 25 turns** — 2026-08-25. Not a defect; a deliberate deletion of working, fully-tested code, filed as a Gap because every code change in this repo needs one. Same shape as Gap 311's Feature 24 removal, and for the same kind of reason: the requirement it answered had been met more cheaply elsewhere by the time it was measured.

  **The evidence, which is the whole justification.** First-ever run of `ENABLE_AGENTIC_SAGE` against real Postgres + real Chroma + a real question bank (25 questions × 2 paths = 50 real turns, 0 errors, 0 cache-served turns, judged by `services/agent_eval.score_answer` at the standard 0.80/0.70/0.70 floors — full method in the Feature 21 § "Phase 3" entry above): **default 23/25, SAGE 19/25. SAGE answered ZERO questions correctly that Feature 6's current default path got wrong; the default path answered four that SAGE got wrong (Q11, Q15, Q19, Q24).** Cost: **+137% LLM calls, +91% tokens-in, +85% tokens-out, +87% cost/turn, +90% median latency** (18.9s → 35.9s median, 54.4s → 101.7s max); `sage.planner` alone burned 285,970 input tokens across 70 calls, more than the entire default path's 25 turns (235,230), and `tool_call_budget_exhausted` fired on **8 of 25 turns** against `MAX_TOOL_CALLS = 4` — a budget that binds routinely is not a safety valve. Two defects, one of them a class the cheap path does not have at all: (1) SAGE lost conversational scope on a narrowing follow-up (Q11 pulled a Dec-2025 invoice into a "Q1 2026 hardware" follow-up set) — on the path whose *stated* advantage is multi-hop reasoning; (2) SAGE **leaked internal tool caveats into user-facing answers on 5 of 25 turns** (*"soft-deleted rows were not excluded"*, *"which invoice statuses count toward spend is not a settled decision"*), i.e. spoke its own unresolved product decisions aloud to the user. The default path leaked none. Honest reading of the margin, recorded rather than rounded away: three of SAGE's four losses were faithfulness-floor failures on answers the accuracy judge scored 1.0/1.0/0.92, so on an accuracy-only reading it is 23 vs 22 — which still leaves SAGE ahead on nothing while costing nearly twice as much. One run per path, not a repeated-trial mean.

  **Why the result came out this way, stated plainly**: Gaps 310 and 315 had already retrofitted SAGE's two genuinely load-bearing ideas — the whole-ORM-row fetch and LLM-free arithmetic — onto the default route, deterministically and without an extra model round-trip. Container health is one Azure Resource Graph query (the same `resources | where type =~ "microsoft.app/containerapps"` projection the panel runs) plus one Azure Monitor metrics read per app, both through the existing `azure_cost.arm_request()` — one managed-identity/CLI token chain in this repo, not two. The metrics parse mirrors the panels exactly: newest **non-null** hourly average for CPU/memory/replicas (Azure returns the in-flight bucket all-null, and reading that as "no data" would blank the panel once an hour), `sum(total)` across 24h for restarts.

- `[x]` **Gap 319 (BE): persistence for the recommendation pass — nothing survived past one run** — closed 2026-08-25. A Workbook can only read Log Analytics / App Insights / Resource Graph / ARM / ADX, **not Postgres**, so this is a custom-event mirror, the same established pattern as `agent_eval_run` / `online_eval_signal`.

  **The event Gap 320 must query: `ops_recommendation`** (`telemetry.OPS_RECOMMENDATION_EVENT_NAME`, emitted by the new `telemetry.track_ops_recommendation()`). **One row per category per run — three rows a night, not one row carrying a three-element array.** That is not a stylistic preference: a workbook grid is a flat row set and Gap 320's columns are `Category | Status | Explanation | Recommendation`, i.e. one row per category already, so the nested form would make every panel `mv-expand` before it could filter or colour on `status`. It is the same call `online_eval_signal` made in choosing one row per signal over one per window.

  **Full field schema** (flat, one `customDimensions` entry each): `run_label`, `category` (`container_health`/`cost`/`ai_improvement`), `title`, `status` (`worked`/`recommend`/`no_data`/`insufficient_data`), `explanation`, `recommendation`, `worst_severity` (`red`/`yellow`/`""`), `finding_count`, `red_count`, `yellow_count`, `findings` (a JSON array serialised as a string, entries `{field, value, severity, detail, recommendation}`), `findings_omitted`, `error_count`, `errors` (the category's error list joined with ` | `), `generated_at`.

  **Four decisions inside that schema.** (1) **`generated_at` is the run key** — set once by the pass and stamped byte-identically on all three rows, so "the latest run" is one `arg_max(generated_at, …)` and can never return two categories from one run and one from another; `TimeGenerated` is ingestion time and is deliberately not that key. (2) **The counts travel next to the blob** so a panel can count reds without `parse_json` + `mv-expand`, and so a trend across a *window* of runs is buildable at all — the same reason `extraction_benchmark_run` carries raw confusion-matrix cells alongside its derived ratios. (3) **`findings` is bounded so that it stays parseable.** Application Insights caps a single property value at 8,192 characters and cuts a longer one *mid-object* at ingestion, which silently turns the array into non-JSON; so the cut is made here instead — ≤25 entries (`MAX_RECOMMENDATION_FINDINGS`), each string field truncated at 400 chars, then whole entries dropped from the end until the serialised text fits 8,000 (`MAX_RECOMMENDATION_FINDINGS_CHARS`), with one same-shaped `{"field": "(omitted)", …}` marker entry appended stating how many went. `explanation`/`recommendation`/`errors` use this module's existing `_truncate()` marker at 2,000 chars, the `MAX_TURN_SQL_CHARS`/`MAX_TURN_TOOL_OUTPUT_CHARS` precedent. (4) **`metrics` is the one field of `to_dict()` not mirrored** — unbounded by design (a dict per container app) and every number in it already has its own event and panel (`azure_cost_snapshot`, `agent_eval_summary`, live Azure Monitor metrics); this event carries the verdict and the fields that produced it, which is what nothing else can say. **No `tenant_id`/`request_id`**, matching `agent_eval_summary` / `extraction_benchmark_run` / `azure_cost_snapshot` / `ops_digest_run` rather than the per-turn events: a scheduled ops pass has no request and no tenant in scope, and an always-empty column invites a join that can never match. The two severity strings are restated as literals in `telemetry.py` rather than imported (nothing there imports from `services/`) and pinned equal to `ops_recommendation.SEVERITY_RED/YELLOW` by test, because a drift would silently zero `red_count` on every event.

  **Query shape**, matching the founder-approved design exactly: `let rows = AppEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where Name == "ops_recommendation" | extend d = parse_json(Properties) | extend run_ts = todatetime(tostring(d.generated_at)); let latest_run = toscalar(rows | summarize max(run_ts)); rows | where run_ts == latest_run | project Category = tostring(d["title"]), Status = tostring(d.status), Explanation = tostring(d.explanation), Recommendation = iff(isempty(tostring(d.recommendation)), "No recommendation yet", tostring(d.recommendation)), Findings = toint(d.finding_count), Red = toint(d.red_count), Yellow = toint(d.yellow_count), Errors = tostring(d.errors), Run = strcat(tostring(d.run_label), " @ ", tostring(d.generated_at)) | order by Category asc`. Global max via `toscalar(... | summarize max(run_ts))`, not `arg_max(...) by category` — one run or zero rows, never a mix. `run_ts` computed via `extend` before `summarize`, never inlined. Run key is `generated_at`, never `TimeGenerated`. No `run_label` filter (emission already nightly-gated upstream). `Errors` projected, not dropped. "No recommendation yet" is rendered literally whenever `d.recommendation` is empty — never inferred from data volume, no extra minimum-sample guard layered on top (the emitter already guarantees the contract per Gaps 318/319).

  **What it is.** Both workbooks (`infra/monitoring/cost_health_workbook.json`, `infra/monitoring/ai_control_tower_workbook.json`) are reorganised onto one shared 3-tier structure, ordered by the founder's stated priority: **Tier 1 Cost & Reliability** (cost awareness / reliability / speed) → **Tier 2 Extraction & Chat Quality** (extraction quality / chat quality nightly / chat quality real usage) → **Tier 3 Cost Reduction** (where cost concentrates). Cost *reduction* is deliberately last despite being the most built-out area today — today's page is ordered by build effort, not by what has to be read first. The `ops_recommendation` cards move **inline into each tier next to the data they explain** (filtered on the event's `category`), replacing Gap 320's single bottom-of-page grid — the founder was explicit that burying recommendations at the end is a real usability problem.

- `[x]` **Gap 323 (Code): `SCORE_BANDS` recalibrated for `pass_rate` and `accuracy` — the two bands that were tuned to what the system scores, not to what "good" means** — closed 2026-08-26. This is Fix 11 of the workbook-redesign fix list (entry above), split out because it is production code. **Scope was the Python constant and its tests only**; the two workbook `thresholdsGrid`s are deliberately untouched and are infra-devops's mirror task.

  **The defect.** `services/ops_recommendation.py::SCORE_BANDS` copied `d1-latest-pass-rate` (red `<0.20`, yellow `<0.30`) and `d2-accuracy` (red `<0.40`, yellow `<0.55`) from the tiles, and both tiles had been calibrated against whatever the system happened to be scoring when they were written. The consequence, measured on the 2026-08-26 nightly run: a real **25.7% pass rate** rendered yellow-at-best and a real **0.600 accuracy** rendered **green**. A coloured tile that cannot report a bad number as bad has no function.

  **New values:**

  | Band | Was | **Now** |
  |---|---|---|
  | `SCORE_BANDS["pass_rate"]` | `(0.20, 0.30)` | **`(0.60, 0.75)`** |
  | `SCORE_BANDS["accuracy"]` | `(0.40, 0.55)` | **`(0.75, 0.90)`** |

  No other `SCORE_BANDS` entry was touched — faithfulness, relevance, context and orchestration still mirror their tiles exactly, as do the CPU/memory, budget, cost-per-turn, alert-recall, FP-rate and error-rate constants.

  **Why these numbers, since this is a judgement call and not a derivation.** *accuracy* is the only dimension graded against a **known-correct reference answer** — faithfulness and relevance are reference-free judge scores where some spread belongs to the judge, not the product — so its bar is held above faithfulness's `(0.70, 0.85)`. Its red bound is anchored rather than picked: `services/agent_eval.py::decide_pass()` already requires `accuracy >= ACCURACY_FLOOR = 0.70` on **every** turn, so a run whose *mean* accuracy sits under that floor means the average turn is failing the gate outright; red therefore starts just above the floor at 0.75, so the mean has to clear it with a margin instead of sitting on it. Yellow at 0.90 is the working target — roughly nine right answers in ten with room left for judge noise — deliberately short of relevance's near-free 0.95. *pass_rate* is the strictest and the only **conjunctive** number the system produces: `decide_pass()` passes a turn only if faithfulness ≥ 0.80 **and** relevance ≥ 0.70 **and** accuracy ≥ 0.70, all on the same turn. That compounding is exactly why its bar is not simply the highest one in the table — three dimensions each clearing their floor on ~90% of turns still lands the joint rate well below 0.90 with no regression at all, so an 0.85-style bar would flag a genuinely healthy system every night and be tuned out inside a week. Green ≥ 0.75 = three turns in four clean on all three checks; yellow 0.60–0.75 = a majority pass but about one in three fails something; red < 0.60 = more than two in five fail a required check, which is not a shippable product. Net shape: `pass_rate` now carries the **lowest yellow** of any band in the module (0.75) because it is the only conjunction, but **not** the lowest red, because a red pass rate is the loudest single statement this module can make.

  **No minimum-run guard is needed for either band to be honest**, and the module already makes that argument one level down — the `context_drift` exemption comment in `evaluate_ai_improvement()` ("a fixed, exhaustive, deterministic script set — the same handful of pinned checks every night, with no sampling error to guard against"). The same reasoning applies to the workbook's n=3-**run** guard on the golden bank, but removing that guard is JSON and was **not** done here. The n=20 **graded-turns** guard (`MIN_GRADED_TURNS`) is a different thing and stays — that one is about how few turns a given run graded, which genuinely can be small.

  **The test-pinning gap this also closed.** `test_ops_recommendation.py::test_each_band_is_still_the_live_panels_band` pinned `d1-latest-pass-rate` to the constant but had **no `d2-accuracy` entry at all**, even though `SCORE_BANDS["accuracy"]` mirrored that tile exactly — so retuning either side would have diverged in silence. `d2-accuracy` is now in the parametrize list.

  **The transitional state, which is deliberate and self-clearing.** The constant moved and the JSON did not (out of scope here), so the two are genuinely inconsistent until infra-devops mirrors them. Rather than delete the pin (next drift goes unnoticed) or leave the suite red (the signal stops meaning anything), both params carry `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` plus a new `test_the_two_recalibrated_bands_still_await_their_json_mirror` that asserts the live grid is still *exactly* the old `(0.20, 0.30)` / `(0.40, 0.55)` — so a third wrong value written into the grid is caught too, which a bare `xfail` would not catch. When infra mirrors the JSON, the two params XPASS, which `strict=True` reports as a failure, forcing removal of both markers and that transitional test.

  **Also flagged, not fixed — a second unpinned copy of these numbers.** `infra/alert-ai-eval-critical-only.bicep` (Gap 299) hardcodes the red bands as parameter defaults (`passRateRedBelow = '0.20'`, `accuracyRedBelow = '0.40'`), plus the same values inside the alert's `description` string and its header comment. **No test pins that file**, so it fails silently: the critical alert would keep firing on the old permissive bands while the tile and the recommendation pass use the new ones. It needs `'0.60'` / `'0.75'` in the same infra pass. Not touched here — bicep is infra scope and needs a real deploy.

Both workbook `thresholdsGrid`s mirrored the same pass; `test_each_band_is_still_the_live_panels_band`'s two `d1`/`d2-accuracy` params XPASSed as predicted, and the transitional `_AWAITING_JSON_MIRROR` markers + `test_the_two_recalibrated_bands_still_await_their_json_mirror` were removed per this entry's own handover note. - `[x]` **Gap 330 (BE): PDF field-highlight overlay renders as tiny dots pinned in the top-left corner instead of boxes over the real fields — both inbound and outbound** — founder-flagged 2026-08-27 via a screenshot of the Auditor Review Console (VPI-OUT-2012): a cluster of near-invisible green dots stacked in the corner, not boxes over the vendor name/line items/totals.
  - **Root cause, confirmed in code.** `queue_worker/handlers.py::_run_ocr()` reads each field's position from Document Intelligence's `bounding_regions[].polygon` and stores the raw min/max values directly (`x_min`, `y_max - y_min`, etc.) with no unit conversion. Document Intelligence returns polygon points in the page's own physical unit — inches for `prebuilt-invoice` — never a 0-100 percentage. `components/audit/PdfViewerCanvas.tsx` has always positioned overlay boxes with `left: ${coord.x}%` / `width: ${coord.width}%`, i.e. it has always assumed the stored value already *is* a percentage. A real value like `x=1.0in` on an 8.5in-wide page rendered as `"1% from the left, 1% wide"` — every box collapsed to a sliver pinned near the origin, regardless of the field's true position. Never caught before because this code path (raw polygon → `coordinates` list) had **zero existing test coverage** — confirmed by grepping the whole test suite for `coordinates_list`/`bounding_regions`/`polygon` before writing this fix.
  - **Confirmed single shared code path, so one fix covers both directions.** `queue_worker/outbound_handlers.py` imports and calls the exact same `_run_ocr()` (`from queue_worker.handlers import _run_ocr`) — not a duplicated copy. Inbound and outbound extraction have been equally affected since coordinates existed; this was never an outbound-only bug, the screenshot just happened to be an outbound invoice.
  - **Fix.** Build a `{page_number: (width, height)}` lookup from Document Intelligence's own `result.pages[]` (reported in the same unit as the polygon points, by construction of the API) before the field loop, then normalize every coordinate against its own page's dimensions: `x = (x_min / page_w) * 100`, and the equivalent for `y`/`width`/`height`, rounded to 3 decimals. A field whose `page_number` has no matching `pages[]` entry (dimensions genuinely unknown) is **dropped, not stored with a guessed unit** — silently misrendering one field's box is worse than omitting it.
  - **Not a data-loss bug, but not self-healing either.** Only the overlay position was ever wrong — the extracted field *values* (vendor name, totals, etc.) were always correct, since those come from the LLM extraction step, not the coordinate math. This fix only corrects coordinates for invoices processed *after* it deploys; every invoice already in the database has the bad percentages already baked into its `coordinates` column and will keep showing the broken overlay until re-extracted. A backfill (re-running Doc Intelligence + re-normalizing for existing rows) is a real, separate cost/scope decision, deliberately not bundled into this fix — flagging it rather than silently leaving it undiscussed.
  - **Tests added — this code path had none before.** `tests/test_extraction.py`: `test_run_ocr_normalizes_coordinates_to_percentage` exercises the real `_run_ocr()` Azure branch (not a mocked black box, unlike every other test in this file) against a fake `AnalyzeResult` shaped like the real SDK response — an 8.5in×11in page, a field polygon at 1.0-3.0in × 1.0-1.5in — and asserts the stored percentages are mathematically exact (`x≈11.765`, `y≈9.091`, `width≈23.529`, `height≈4.545`) and every value lands in `[0, 100]`. `test_run_ocr_skips_coordinate_when_page_dimensions_missing` asserts a field on a page with no matching `pages[]` entry is dropped, not stored wrong.
  - **Verification**: `pytest tests/test_extraction.py` — **9 passed** (7 pre-existing + the 2 new ones above), real Postgres, not SQLite. Live before/after screenshot proof of a re-extracted invoice's overlay boxes landing on the real fields, to be appended here once deployed.
  - **Live-verified 2026-08-27, math confirmed correct — but the FE display was subsequently removed.** A real post-deploy invoice (`INV-2025-0019`, created 10:50 UTC) showed the coordinate *data* is now genuinely right — `VendorName` and `InvoiceId` share nearly identical `y` (10.688 vs 10.712), matching that they sit on the same line in the real document. The remaining visual imprecision traced to a separate, harder problem: `PdfViewerCanvas.tsx` renders the PDF via a native `<iframe>`, which doesn't guarantee its rendered content fills the frame at the same aspect ratio the percentage math assumes — a correct fix needs a canvas-based renderer (pdf.js), real separate scope. Founder chose to drop the overlay display rather than ship the imprecision — see **FE Gap 318** for the removal. This backend fix was **not** reverted: coordinates are still computed and stored correctly on every new extraction, just not rendered anywhere right now — free to keep, and means a future pdf.js-based viewer wouldn't need re-extraction to use them.

- `[x]` **Gap 334 (BE): Remove the Salesforce connector entirely — cross-org OAuth is structurally blocked, and the data model was wrong for invoices anyway** — founder decision 2026-08-28. **Gap number collision-checked before writing**: the true current max in this file is `Gap 333` (332 is unused/skipped), so 334 is free; the FE half of this removal is filed separately as **FE Gap 322** (checked the same way against that tracker's max of 321). Filed **before** any code change, per this repo's no-code-without-gap rule — this entry is the scope of record, not a post-hoc writeup.
  - **Root cause 1 — technical, and not fixable by any setting.** The Salesforce OAuth app backing this connector is a Salesforce **External Client App** with **Distribution State = Local**, which by design permits authorization only from the org that created the app. Every other org is refused at the authorize step. Confirmed live, not inferred: a Log Analytics query against `ca-invoice-be-dev` returned Salesforce's real error, `OAUTH_AUTHORIZATION_BLOCKED — Cross-org OAuth flows are not supported for this external client app`. Since a multi-tenant SaaS connector's entire premise is that *other* orgs authorize against one shared company app, this is a structural block, not a misconfiguration — there is no toggle that makes a Local-distribution external client app serve foreign orgs. The obvious workaround (fall back to a classic Connected App, which is what Task 9.5 and Gap 98 originally built against) is also closed: Salesforce stopped allowing creation of new classic Connected Apps as of **Spring '26** absent a support exception. Both doors are shut at the same time.
  - **Root cause 2 — product fit, independent of the above.** Even a working connection would surface almost nothing useful. This connector's file browsing is scoped to Salesforce **Libraries** (`ContentWorkspace`) — that was Gap 262's deliberate design — but in real Salesforce orgs, invoices are not filed in Libraries; they arrive as attachments on **Account/Opportunity** records. Salesforce is a CRM, not a document or billing system for most orgs. So the connector browses the one place invoices reliably are *not*. This is the more important of the two causes: it means fixing the OAuth block would not have produced a feature worth shipping, and it is why the decision is *remove* rather than *park until Salesforce support grants an exception*.
  - **Removal scope — this Gap (BE only).** Code: `utils/connector_files.py` (the 4 Salesforce functions + `SALESFORCE_API_VERSION`), `utils/connector_oauth.py` (`SALESFORCE_TOKEN_URL`, `generate_pkce_pair()`, the Salesforce arms of `has_real_credentials`/token refresh, the `instance_url` write-back), `queue_worker/handlers.py`, `services/autopilot_sync.py`, `routers/autopilot.py`, `routers/connectors.py` (all 5 endpoint handlers, plus the now-dead PKCE plumbing Gap 98's third follow-up added), `config.py`, `models.py` (comments only), `agents/support_agent.py`. Tests: `tests/test_connectors.py`. Docs: `feature_9_connectors.md` and the other Salesforce-mentioning specs, annotated/struck rather than rewritten (hard rule 4). Tracker: this entry plus one-line supersede annotations on Gaps 98, 197, 261, 262 — annotated, never deleted, since they are the institutional record of why the plumbing existed.
  - **Deliberately NOT in this Gap's scope, and not silently done anyway.** (a) **Everything under `infra/`** — `05-secrets.bicep`'s `SALESFORCE-CLIENT-SECRET`, `08-apps.bicep`, `invoice-be.bicep`/`queue-worker.bicep` env wiring, `params.dev.json`/`params.dev.secrets.json`/`params.prod.json`, and the live Azure resources (Key Vault secret, Container App env vars) they produce. That is actively false today, independent of when the rest of the removal lands.

These structures must be edited surgically, never deleted wholesale; **Google Drive is the one connector that actually works and must not regress.** Same hazard in `services/autopilot_sync.py`, where the download path is an `if gdrive / else salesforce` — deleting only the `else` arm leaves a conditional with no fallback, so it has to collapse into unconditional Drive-only code.

- `[x]` **Gap 343 (BE, Feature 11 / billing): the free-tier invoice quota is enforced on one ingest door out of four — Drive import, Autopilot sync and outbound upload all bypass it entirely** — found 2026-08-30 while scoping Feature 25, **filed against Feature 11 (billing), not Feature 25**: it is a pre-existing spend-side defect that has nothing to do with plug-and-play, it was simply noticed during that feature's route audit. Spec: [feature_11_billing.md](feature_11_billing.md).
  - **Gap number collision-checked fresh, not inherited.** Re-grepped at filing time with parallel FE work in flight: true max in *this* tracker is **Gap 337**, and a repo-wide grep for the literal `Gap 343` across every `.md`/`.py`/`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.json` (excluding `node_modules`/`.venv`) returned exactly one hit — `PLUG_AND_PLAY_STATUS.md`, a loop-status file that pre-assigns this number to this work. The website tracker explicitly reserves 335–344 for the two in-flight parallel builds, so 343 is free by that file's own rule too.
  - **The problem, stated precisely.** Gap 189 established the correct charge path — `count_billable_uploads()` (classify hashes first, so a duplicate never burns quota) then `charge_free_quota()` (`SELECT tenant … FOR UPDATE`, decrement only the billable count, `402 "Limit reached"` when the balance is short). It was wired into `routers/invoices.py` only: `upload_invoices()` and `start_directory_watcher()`. **Three other doors create `Invoice` rows and charge nothing**: `routers/connectors.py::trigger_file_import()` (manual Google Drive import), `services/autopilot_sync.py::run_sync()` (scheduled Drive polling, which also runs unattended from an ACA Job), and `routers/outbound_invoices.py::upload_outbound_invoice()`. A Free Tier tenant with `free_invoices_remaining = 0` could therefore ingest without limit by connecting Drive and clicking Import, or by letting Autopilot poll — the 50/month cap held only against whoever happened to use the direct upload button. `free_invoices_remaining` could sit at 0 while invoices kept arriving; **the counter never went negative, because it was never touched at all**, which is why nothing in the existing metrics would have shown this.
  - **Exhaustion behaviour is mirrored, not invented.** `routers/invoices.py` rejects with `402 "Limit reached"` and ingests nothing. The two HTTP doors do exactly that — `charge_free_quota()` raises the identical exception, so the connector import is refused **before** the queue message is sent and the outbound upload is refused **before** the blob is written. The scheduled sync has no HTTP caller to 402, so it does the equivalent: the file is not ingested, a `FAILED` `TenantAutopilotLog` row records the reason, and the loop stops (every remaining file would fail for the same reason, and downloading them anyway would burn Drive API calls for nothing). Because `TenantAutopilotLog`'s dedup layer only skips rows with `status == "SUCCESS"`, a file refused on quota is retried on the next cycle once the quota refills (Gap 118) — no manual intervention, and no permanently-skipped file.
  - **A second, real defect fixed in the same change, because the new call sites make it reachable.** `charge_free_quota()`'s locked SELECT did not carry `populate_existing=True`. SQLAlchemy's identity map returns an already-loaded `Tenant` instance **without refreshing its attributes**, so a caller that had loaded the tenant earlier in the same transaction would take the row lock and then evaluate the quota check against a stale in-memory `free_invoices_remaining` — the lock held, the value it was protecting did not. `routers/invoices.py` never hit this (it loads no tenant before charging), but `routers/outbound_invoices.py` loads the `Tenant` up front for its `send_invoices_enabled` check, which is exactly the shape that triggers it. Fixed inside `charge_free_quota()` rather than at the call site, so all five call sites get it and a sixth cannot reintroduce it. `locked_tenant_select()` is unchanged, so `test_ingestion.py::test_charge_free_quota_uses_for_update` still guards the `FOR UPDATE` itself.

That is not a shortcut: the connector path does not persist `Invoice.file_hash` at all, so every connector import already creates a distinct invoice row regardless of content, and charging 1 per import is the *accurate* count for that door. Charging in the worker instead was rejected — the worker cannot return a 402 to anybody, so a quota refusal there would be an invisible background failure, which is the exact class of bug Gaps 179/180/266 were opened for on this same code path.

A throwaway script against real local Postgres (`localhost:5433/invoice_db`) created its own free-plan tenant, asserted, and deleted everything it made — 0 rows left behind. What it proved, in order: `charge_free_quota` decrementing on the real database (3 → 2); **`FOR UPDATE` genuinely holding the row** — a second connection issuing `SELECT … FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` against it was refused with `LockNotAvailable`, which SQLite cannot express at all since `.with_for_update()` compiles to nothing there; **the stale identity-map read reproduced and then fixed** — with the tenant already loaded in the session and the value changed to 0 by another connection, the locked SELECT *without* `populate_existing` still returned the stale `2`, and *with* it returned the real `0`; an exhausted tenant raising `HTTPException 402 "Limit reached"` with the row unchanged at 0 afterwards; and `run_sync()` itself, run against the Postgres session, returning `{'processed': 0, 'failed': 1, 'quota_exhausted': True}` with **zero `Invoice` rows created** and one `FAILED` log naming the quota — then, after the counter was topped up, the same call returning `processed: 1` and decrementing correctly.   - **Gap number collision-checked fresh, not inherited from cached numbers.** Re-grepped at filing time (335–343 all landed in this tracker in the last two days, so any cached max was stale): true current max in *this* tracker is **Gap 343**, and 338 was the one number in that run never used.
